Decomposition API reference#

See Decompositions for the source-to-engine workflow, examples and help choosing an algorithm or strategy. This page lists the public objects by responsibility. Matrix and Quantics representations are documented in Formats.

Input sources#

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.BaseSource(n_sites, n_batches=0, *, in_sites=None)[source]#

Common interface and shared operations for decomposition input data.

Sources let decomposition algorithms query tensors or callables through the same interface, independently of how their values are stored or computed. Concrete sources adapt dense tensors, sparse tensors, formats or functions; the algorithm defines how to approximate those values.

The main operation is evaluate(), which receives a ConfigurationBatch with one column per entry of in_sites containing discrete indices or continuous features, and returns values with shape (batch, *core_batch, *out_shape), preserving their order. core_batch denotes optional structural batch dimensions, independent of the queried configurations and represented variables.

Sources record successful queries with _record_evaluation; evaluation_stats exposes cumulative counters so algorithms can measure their evaluation cost. Recording does not cache values or deduplicate configurations automatically.

Properties describe the evaluated data: in_dim bounds discrete indices, out_shape describes each returned value, and dtype and device specify its numerical representation. out_shape and dtype may be inferred on first evaluation. Continuous sources normally have in_dim=None; matrix grouping alone does not discretize a callable. Vector in_dim contains every variable dimension, and in_sites selects the evaluated subset. Matrix dimensions describe one input/output pair per variable; every pair receives an input. is_discrete_tensor distinguishes finite indexed tensors.

Two shared operations build on evaluation: fiber() varies one input site while fixing the others, and contract_dense() evaluates the complete tensor when is_discrete_tensor=True. Subclasses may replace these generic implementations with specialized contractions.

To implement a source, provide evaluate() and the abstract data properties, and call super().__init__(n_sites, in_sites=...) to declare all represented variables and the ordered evaluated inputs. Sources supply values and evaluation information; they do not define a fitting loss or decide which entries are missing.

Parameters

  • n_sites (int) – Total number of represented variables. A matrix variable has one input axis and one output axis.

  • n_batches (int, optional) – Number of structural batch axes, whose sizes form core_batch. Defaults to 0.

  • in_sites (sequence of int, optional) – Ordered variables received by evaluation configurations. The complement supplies the output axes. Defaults to all variables; matrices always evaluate every variable and return their paired output axes.

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.DenseTensorSource(torch.ones(2, 3))
>>> source.contract_dense()
tensor([[1., 1., 1.],
        [1., 1., 1.]])
property n_sites#

Total number of represented variables, including output variables.

property is_matrix#

Whether local axes are paired as matrix inputs and outputs.

property is_discrete_tensor#

Whether all configurations index a fixed finite tensor.

abstract property in_dim#

Dimensions of all vector variables or each matrix pair’s input axis.

None when no finite index grid is defined.

property out_dim#

Output dimension of each matrix pair, or None for vectors.

property in_sites#

Ordered variables evaluated by the configuration columns.

property out_shape#

Response dimensions, excluding query and structural batch axes.

Vectors retain the dimensions outside in_sites in their original variable order. Matrices return all out_dim axes. Callable sources may return None until the response shape is known.

abstract property dtype#

Output dtype, or None until a callable source is evaluated.

abstract property device#

Device on which evaluations are performed.

property evaluation_stats#

Cumulative point-evaluation counters for this source.

abstract evaluate(configurations)[source]#

Evaluates configurations in their original order.

Parameters

configurations (ConfigurationBatch) – Discrete indices of shape (batch, len(in_sites)), or continuous features of shape (batch, len(in_sites), *feature_shape). A heterogeneous batch contains len(in_sites) tensors. Columns and sequence entries follow in_sites order.

Returns

Values with shape (batch, *core_batch, *out_shape) on the source device and with its declared or inferred dtype. Evaluation retains the source’s autograd behavior; diagnostic counters do not change the returned values.

Return type

torch.Tensor

fiber(configurations, site, values=None)[source]#

Evaluates a source while varying one site of each configuration.

For example, if a scalar source represents f(i, j) and a base configuration is (i=1, j=0), setting site=1 and values=[0, 1, 2] returns [f(1, 0), f(1, 1), f(1, 2)] for that configuration. Other configurations in the batch are expanded in the same way, without changing their order.

Parameters

  • configurations (ConfigurationBatch) – Base configurations with len(in_sites) inputs per row, ordered by in_sites. Packed indices have shape (batch, len(in_sites)); features may add trailing feature axes or use a tuple with one tensor per input. Only the column in_sites.index(site) is varied; all other inputs remain fixed.

  • site (int) – Represented variable whose value varies; it must belong to in_sites.

  • values (torch.Tensor, optional) – Candidate values for the selected site. Discrete indices have shape (n_values,); features have shape (n_values, *feature_shape[in_sites.index(site)]). If omitted for discrete indices, every index in range(in_dim[site]) is evaluated. Feature fibers require explicit values.

Returns

Values with shape (batch, n_values, *core_batch, *out_shape). The first axis follows the input configurations; the second follows values (or increasing discrete indices when omitted).

Return type

torch.Tensor

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.CallableTensorSource(
...     lambda indices: indices.sum(-1).float(), in_dim=(2, 3))
>>> configurations = tk.decompositions.ConfigurationBatch(
...     torch.tensor([[1, 0]]))
>>> source.fiber(configurations, site=1)
tensor([[1., 2., 3.]])
contract_dense()[source]#

Evaluates the complete finite tensor in its represented axis order.

Returns

Shape (*core_batch, *in_dim) for vectors, with variables in their original order regardless of in_sites. Matrices return shape (*core_batch, in_0, out_0, in_1, out_1, ...), pairing input and output axes in site order. Continuous sources require an explicit finite discretization.

Return type

torch.Tensor

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.CallableTensorSource(
...     lambda indices: indices.sum(-1).float(), in_dim=(2, 2))
>>> source.contract_dense()
tensor([[0., 1.],
        [1., 2.]])
class tensorkrowch.decompositions.ConfigurationBatch(values, kind='indices')[source]#

Batch of discrete indices or possibly continuous features.

values can be a packed tensor with shape (batch, n_inputs), or a sequence of n_inputs tensors. For source evaluation, n_inputs = len(source.in_sites) and columns follow source.in_sites. The batch’s n_inputs returns this column count, which can be smaller than source.n_sites.

For kind="indices", each column holds one integer index. For kind="features", each column holds a scalar or tensor-valued feature passed to a callable. A packed feature batch has shape (batch, n_inputs, *feature_shape); the sequence form permits different feature shapes for each input. kind applies to the entire batch.

Parameters

  • values (torch.Tensor or sequence of torch.Tensor) – Packed configurations or one tensor per evaluated input, in in_sites order. All tensors in a heterogeneous batch share their leading batch dimension, device and dtype.

  • kind ({"indices", "features"}) – Meaning of the values at every input. "indices" is the default and requires scalar integers. "features" accepts scalar or tensor-valued inputs for callables.

property packed#

Whether all inputs are stored in one tensor.

property batch_size#

Number of configurations in the batch.

property n_inputs#

Input column count; equals len(source.in_sites) for source queries.

property device#

Device shared by the configuration values.

property dtype#

Data type shared by the configuration values.

property feature_shape#

Feature shape per input column, or None for discrete indices.

as_tensor()[source]#

Returns a packed tensor when all input shapes are compatible.

index_select(indices)[source]#

Selects configurations along the batch dimension.

to(device)[source]#

Returns the configurations on device without changing dtype.

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.DenseTensorSource(tensor, n_batches=0, *, in_sites=None)[source]#

Tensor source backed by an explicitly stored dense tensor.

The usual constructor represents a tensor with one axis per vector site. By default, evaluate() receives one integer index per axis and returns a scalar for each configuration. Pass in_sites to evaluate only some axes: configurations have shape (batch, len(in_sites)) in that selection’s order, and the remaining axes form out_shape in their original order. Leading structural batch axes are excluded from the variable numbering. n_sites counts all non-batch axes, including those returned as outputs.

Use matrix() instead to represent a matrix with one input/output axis pair per site. The tensor must already have its input/output axes separated; a two-axis tensor represents a single site. This grouping sets is_matrix=True and provides in_dim and out_dim for matrix decompositions. A matrix source evaluates the input indices and returns all output axes, with out_shape == out_dim.

Parameters

  • tensor (torch.Tensor) – Dense tensor containing input and optional output axes.

  • n_batches (int) – Number of leading structural batch axes. Defaults to 0.

  • in_sites (sequence of int, optional) – Distinct non-batch axes, in configuration order. Defaults to all non-batch axes in increasing order.

Examples

>>> tensor = torch.arange(6.).reshape(2, 3)
>>> source = tk.decompositions.DenseTensorSource(tensor)
>>> source.evaluate(tk.decompositions.ConfigurationBatch(
...     torch.tensor([[1, 2]])))
tensor([5.])

Keeping the second axis as output returns a vector per configuration:

>>> source = tk.decompositions.DenseTensorSource(tensor, in_sites=(0,))
>>> source.out_shape
(3,)
>>> source.evaluate(tk.decompositions.ConfigurationBatch(
...     torch.tensor([[1]])))
tensor([[3., 4., 5.]])
classmethod matrix(tensor, *, ordering='grouped')[source]#

Constructs a paired matrix source from dense matrix or tensor axes.

Each site has an input dimension in_dim[i] and an output dimension out_dim[i]. Input indices are evaluated together; the returned tensor contains every output axis in site order. evaluate() receives shape (batch, n_sites) in site order and returns all output axes, with out_shape == out_dim.

The tensor must have an even number of axes, with one input/output pair per site. ordering="interleaved" means axes (in_0, out_0, in_1, out_1, ...); ordering="grouped" means axes (in_0, in_1, ..., out_0, out_1, ...). Local dimensions are inferred directly from these axes. A two-axis tensor represents one site; separate its axes explicitly with reshape to represent more sites. Structural batch axes are not supported by this constructor.

The source exposes paired dimensions and contract_dense() returns the tensor with interleaved axes, regardless of input ordering.

Parameters

  • tensor (torch.Tensor) – Tensor with explicit input/output axes in the specified ordering.

  • ordering ({"grouped", "interleaved"}) – Ordering of tensorized axes; defaults to "grouped".

Returns

Matrix source with out_shape == out_dim.

Return type

DenseTensorSource

Examples

Explicitly separate a matrix into two sites before constructing the source:

>>> source = tk.decompositions.DenseTensorSource.matrix(
...     torch.eye(4).reshape(2, 2, 2, 2))
>>> source.evaluate(tk.decompositions.ConfigurationBatch(
...     torch.tensor([[0, 1]])))
tensor([[[0., 1.],
         [0., 0.]]])

Infer dimensions from grouped axes, then retrieve interleaved axes:

>>> source = tk.decompositions.DenseTensorSource.matrix(
...     torch.arange(24.).reshape(2, 3, 2, 2))
>>> source.in_dim, source.out_dim
((2, 3), (2, 2))
>>> source.contract_dense().shape
torch.Size([2, 2, 3, 2])
property in_dim#

Dimensions of all vector variables or matrix input axes.

property dtype#

Dtype of the stored tensor.

property device#

Device of the stored tensor.

evaluate(configurations)[source]#

Gathers values for integer configurations of shape (batch, len(in_sites)), with columns ordered by in_sites.

contract_dense()[source]#

Returns the stored tensor without copying its tensor storage.

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.SparseTensorSource(indices, values, in_dim, *, in_sites=None)[source]#

Sparse tensor source with declared zeros outside its support.

The usual constructor represents a tensor with one axis per vector site. The source’s in_dim contains every site’s dimension. n_sites counts all sites, including those returned as outputs. in_sites selects the evaluated sites, in configuration order; the remaining axes form out_shape in their original order, as in DenseTensorSource.

Columns of indices and evaluation configurations follow in_sites order. Trailing axes of values are output axes, in the original order of the remaining sites. By default, inputs occupy the first sites.

Repeated indices are coalesced by summing their values, matching sparse COO semantics; boolean values are combined by logical OR. Absent entries are known zeros, rather than missing observations.

Use matrix() for scalar entries with paired input/output indices, or from_data() to construct a vector source representing a normalized empirical distribution. The usual constructor and matrix() preserve the supplied values without normalizing them.

Parameters

  • indices (torch.Tensor) – Integer indices of shape (n_entries, len(in_sites)), with columns ordered by in_sites.

  • values (torch.Tensor) – Stored values of shape (n_entries, *out_shape), with output axes in the original order of sites outside in_sites.

  • in_dim (sequence of int) – Dimensions of all sites in chain order, or only input dimensions in in_sites order when output sites are present. Omitted output dimensions are inferred from the trailing axes of values.

  • in_sites (sequence of int, optional) – Distinct input sites, in configuration order. Defaults to the first indices.shape[1] sites, in increasing order.

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.SparseTensorSource(
...     torch.tensor([[0], [2]]), torch.tensor([2., 5.]), in_dim=(3,))
>>> source.contract_dense()
tensor([2., 0., 5.])

Select only the first variable while retaining the full tensor dimensions:

>>> source = tk.decompositions.SparseTensorSource(
...     torch.tensor([[0], [1]]),
...     torch.tensor([[0., 2., 0.], [0., 0., 5.]]),
...     in_dim=(2, 3), in_sites=(0,))
>>> source.n_sites, source.in_dim, source.out_shape
(2, (2, 3), (3,))
>>> source.evaluate(tk.decompositions.ConfigurationBatch(torch.tensor([[1]])))
tensor([[0., 0., 5.]])
classmethod matrix(indices, values, in_dim, out_dim, *, ordering='grouped')[source]#

Constructs a matrix source from paired input/output entry indices.

Unlike the usual constructor, each row of indices identifies both sides of a scalar matrix entry. By default, columns are grouped as (in_0, in_1, ..., out_0, out_1, ...). With ordering="interleaved", columns alternate as (in_0, out_0, in_1, out_1, ...). For n_sites pairs, in_dim and out_dim must each contain n_sites dimensions; they cannot be inferred from the stored entries alone.

evaluate() receives only input indices, with shape (batch, n_sites) in site order, and returns all output axes with out_shape == out_dim. Unstored entries remain zero. contract_dense() returns interleaved input/output axes regardless of input ordering, as in DenseTensorSource.matrix().

Parameters

  • indices (torch.Tensor) – Integer indices with shape (n_entries, 2 * n_sites) in ordering.

  • values (torch.Tensor) – Scalar entry values with shape (n_entries,).

  • in_dim (sequence of int) – Input and output dimensions, respectively, for each matrix site.

  • out_dim (sequence of int) – Input and output dimensions, respectively, for each matrix site.

  • ordering ({"grouped", "interleaved"}) – Order of index columns; defaults to "grouped".

Returns

Source retaining paired axes for matrix decomposition.

Return type

SparseTensorSource

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.SparseTensorSource.matrix(
...     torch.tensor([[0, 1], [1, 0]]), torch.tensor([2., 3.]),
...     in_dim=(2,), out_dim=(2,))
>>> source.evaluate(tk.decompositions.ConfigurationBatch(
...     torch.tensor([[0]])))
tensor([[0., 2.]])
>>> source.contract_dense()
tensor([[0., 2.],
        [3., 0.]])
classmethod from_data(dataset, in_dim=None, weights=None, dtype=None)[source]#

Constructs a discrete empirical distribution from sample indices.

Each row of dataset is one observation, rather than an entry with an explicitly supplied value as in the usual constructor. Samples receive equal weights by default; explicit weights are normalized to sum to one. Repeated configurations accumulate their weights, and unobserved configurations have zero mass. The result is a scalar vector source with out_shape=().

Parameters

  • dataset (torch.Tensor) – Integer samples with shape (n_samples, len(in_sites)). All columns are inputs in their given order, so this constructor has len(in_sites) == n_sites. Repeats accumulate.

  • in_dim (sequence of int, optional) – Dimensions of all vector sites; inferred from sample maxima when omitted.

  • weights (torch.Tensor, optional) – Non-negative sample weights, normalized to total mass one.

  • dtype (torch.dtype, optional) – Dtype for uniform or integral weights.

Returns

Vector source with known zeros outside the observed support.

Return type

SparseTensorSource

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.SparseTensorSource.from_data(
...     torch.tensor([[0], [2], [0]]), in_dim=(3,))
>>> source.contract_dense()
tensor([0.6667, 0.0000, 0.3333])
property in_dim#

Dimensions of all vector variables or matrix input axes.

property dtype#

Dtype of sparse values.

property device#

Device of sparse indices and values.

property support#

Coalesced stored indices in in_sites order for vectors.

Matrices return interleaved input/output indices in site order.

property support_values#

Stored values corresponding to support.

evaluate(configurations)[source]#

Evaluates integer configurations of shape (batch, len(in_sites)) in in_sites order. Returns shape (batch, *out_shape), with zeros outside the support.

contract_dense()[source]#

Materializes all sites in their original order, with zeros outside the support. Matrix input/output axes are interleaved in site order.

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.FormatSource(format)[source]#

Finite tensor source represented directly by a lightweight format.

Construct the source from a TT, TR or their matrix versions, TTM and TRM. Evaluation and dense contraction use the backing format without first materializing its complete tensor. For vectors, configuration columns have shape (batch, len(in_sites)) in the format’s in_sites order; the remaining axes form out_shape.

Matrix grouping is inferred from the format, so no separate matrix constructor is needed. Matrix evaluations receive indices for every input site and return all output axes, independently of the format’s evaluation defaults, with out_shape == out_dim and len(in_sites) == n_sites.

An MPS is converted to TT or TR, and an MPO to TTM or TRM, according to their boundaries. A sequence of cores instead constructs an open TT. Quantics formats require an explicit CallableQuanticsSource. Environment and sketch contractions require an unbatched open TT with every site selected as an input. Effective cores are prepared for each contraction, with explicit bond factors absorbed.

Parameters

format (TensorFormat1D, MPS, MPO or sequence of torch.Tensor) – Lightweight vector/matrix format, MPS, MPO or raw TT cores. Model boundaries determine the open or cyclic representation.

Examples

>>> format = tk.formats.TT([torch.eye(2), torch.eye(2)])
>>> source = tk.decompositions.FormatSource(format)
>>> source.evaluate(tk.decompositions.ConfigurationBatch(
...     torch.tensor([[0, 0], [0, 1]])))
tensor([1., 0.])

A matrix format already provides the input/output grouping:

>>> format = tk.formats.TTM([torch.eye(2)])
>>> source = tk.decompositions.FormatSource(format)
>>> source.evaluate(tk.decompositions.ConfigurationBatch(
...     torch.tensor([[1]])))
tensor([[0., 1.]])
property in_dim#

Dimensions of all vector variables or matrix input axes.

property dtype#

Dtype of the backing format.

property device#

Device of the backing format.

left_envs(configurations)[source]#

Contracts the first TT sites at fixed indices, leaving their right bond open.

Parameters

configurations (torch.Tensor) – Integer indices with shape (batch, prefix_sites) for the first prefix_sites sites, in chain order. Zero columns select the empty prefix.

Returns

Shape (batch, right_rank), where right_rank is the bond dimension after the prefix. An empty prefix returns ones with shape (batch, 1). Direct contractions do not record point evaluations.

Return type

torch.Tensor

right_envs(configurations)[source]#

Contracts the final TT sites at fixed indices, leaving their left bond open.

Parameters

configurations (torch.Tensor) – Integer indices with shape (batch, suffix_sites) for the final suffix_sites sites, in chain order. Zero columns select the empty suffix.

Returns

Shape (batch, left_rank), where left_rank is the bond dimension before the suffix. An empty suffix returns ones with shape (batch, 1). Direct contractions do not record point evaluations.

Return type

torch.Tensor

local_phi(site, left, right, factor=None)[source]#

Contracts a TT core with left and right sketch environments, leaving its input axis open. Environments are used without conjugation.

Parameters

  • site (int) – Site of the source core.

  • left (torch.Tensor) – Shape (left_size, left_rank). Columns match the core’s left bond; rows identify left sketch coordinates.

  • right (torch.Tensor) – Shape (right_size, right_rank). Columns match the core’s right bond; rows identify right sketch coordinates.

  • factor (torch.Tensor, optional) – Multiplicative input weights of shape (in_dim[site],). None uses unit weights.

Returns

Local Phi with shape (left_size, in_dim[site], right_size).

Return type

torch.Tensor

marginal_phi(site, order=1, factor=None)[source]#

Sums distant TT sites while retaining the central site and its local neighbors for a Markov marginal sketch.

Parameters

  • site (int) – Central site.

  • order (int) – Maximum number of neighboring sites retained on each side, limited by the chain boundaries. Defaults to 1.

  • factor (sequence of torch.Tensor, optional) – One multiplicative weight vector of shape (in_dim[k],) per site k, applied before retaining or summing its input axis. None uses unit weights.

Returns

Shape (left_size, in_dim[site], right_size). Retained neighbors on each side are flattened in chain order into the first and last axes. A side without neighbors has size 1.

Return type

torch.Tensor

tt_sketch_phis(left_cores, right_cores, boundary_scale=1.0)[source]#

Contracts TT sketch stacks with the source to build every local Phi. Sketches are contracted in a batch, reusing prefix and suffix environments across sites. Sketch cores are used without conjugation.

Parameters

  • left_cores (sequence of sequences of torch.Tensor) – TT sketches in the left stack, each with one core per source site. Core k has shape (left_rank, in_dim[k], right_rank), with unit boundary ranks. Sketches share bond dimensions at each cut.

  • right_cores (sequence of sequences of torch.Tensor) – TT sketches in the right stack, with the same layout and number of sketches as left_cores.

  • boundary_scale (float) – Multiplier applied to the first left and last right sketch cores in their environment contractions. Defaults to 1.0.

Returns

One Phi per site k, with shape (left_size, in_dim[k], right_size). Each outer axis combines sketch and bond indices; chain boundary axes have size 1.

Return type

tuple of torch.Tensor

evaluate(configurations)[source]#

Evaluates discrete configurations through the backing format.

Parameters

configurations (ConfigurationBatch) – Integer indices with shape (batch, len(in_sites)) and columns ordered by in_sites. Matrix sources evaluate every paired site.

Returns

Values with shape (batch, *core_batch, *out_shape). Matrix output axes remain open; vectors retain their selected inputs.

Return type

torch.Tensor

fiber(configurations, site, values=None)[source]#

Varies one input site while fixing the other inputs. Uses direct TT environments when available, otherwise BaseSource.fiber().

Parameters

  • configurations (ConfigurationBatch) – Integer indices with shape (batch, len(in_sites)), with columns ordered by in_sites.

  • site (int) – Represented variable to vary; it must belong to in_sites.

  • values (torch.Tensor, optional) – Candidate integer indices with shape (n_values,). None evaluates every index in range(in_dim[site]).

Returns

Shape (batch, n_values, *core_batch, *out_shape). The first axis follows configurations; the second follows candidate values.

Return type

torch.Tensor

contract_dense()[source]#

Contracts the complete backing format in original site order, independently of in_sites.

Returns

Shape (*core_batch, *in_dim) for vectors. Matrices interleave input/output axes as (*core_batch, in_0, out_0, in_1, out_1, ...).

Return type

torch.Tensor

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.CallableSource(function, n_sites, out_shape=None, dtype=None, device='cpu', batch_size=None, *, in_sites=None)[source]#

Continuous function evaluated by a user callable.

Packed configurations are passed to function with shape (batch, len(in_sites), *feature_shape); scalar inputs have no trailing feature axes. Heterogeneous inputs are passed as a tuple of len(in_sites) tensors. Both forms follow in_sites order. The callable preserves the leading batch and returns (batch, *out_shape).

Construct the source with function and its total variable count. in_sites selects the inputs; all remaining variables are output axes. Output shape and dtype can be declared or discovered on first evaluation. This source accepts continuous features and has no finite grid to materialize. Use CallableTensorSource for discrete indices, or CallableQuanticsSource to discretize a coordinate function.

The alternative constructor matrix() pairs each continuous input with an output axis for a function returning all output entries per input. from_data() instead builds a scalar vector source from observed coordinates, using exact matches or a user-supplied kernel.

Parameters

  • function (callable) – Receives the inputs selected by in_sites, in that order, and returns shape (batch, *out_shape).

  • n_sites (int) – Total number of input and output variables. An input variable receives a scalar or embedded vector; each remaining variable is an output axis.

  • out_shape (sequence of int or None, optional) – Declared response shape. The default None discovers it on the first non-empty evaluation; its rank must equal n_sites - len(in_sites). () requires scalar responses.

  • dtype (torch.dtype or None, optional) – Declared output dtype. None infers it from the first evaluation.

  • device (str or torch.device, optional) – Device to which configurations are moved before evaluation. Returned values must use the same device. Defaults to 'cpu'.

  • batch_size (int or None, optional) – Maximum number of configurations passed to one callable invocation.

  • in_sites (sequence of int, optional) – Ordered input variables. Defaults to all variables; output axes follow the complement in increasing variable order.

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.CallableSource(
...     lambda coordinates: coordinates.sum(-1), n_sites=2)
>>> source.evaluate(tk.decompositions.ConfigurationBatch(
...     torch.tensor([[0.25, 0.5], [1., 2.]]), kind='features'))
tensor([0.7500, 3.0000])
classmethod matrix(function, n_sites, out_shape=None, **kwargs)[source]#

Constructs a continuous matrix source with one output axis per input.

evaluate() receives inputs for every site in site order and returns all output axes, with out_shape == out_dim. Each input is continuous, so in_dim remains None. Output dimensions can be declared or inferred on first evaluation; their count must equal n_sites. Output indices are not passed separately.

Parameters

  • function (callable) – Receives shape (batch, n_sites, *feature_shape) or a tuple of n_sites tensors, and returns shape (batch, *out_shape).

  • n_sites (int) – Number of paired continuous inputs and output axes.

  • out_shape (sequence of int or None, optional) – Output dimension for each site. None infers the dimensions from the first non-empty evaluation.

  • **kwargs – dtype, device and batch_size options of CallableSource.

Returns

Matrix source with out_shape == out_dim.

Return type

CallableSource

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.CallableSource.matrix(
...     lambda x: torch.stack((x[:, 0], 1 - x[:, 0]), dim=-1),
...     n_sites=1)
>>> source.evaluate(tk.decompositions.ConfigurationBatch(
...     torch.tensor([[0.25], [0.75]]), kind='features'))
tensor([[0.2500, 0.7500],
        [0.7500, 0.2500]])
>>> source.out_dim
(2,)
classmethod from_data(dataset, weights=None, *, kernel=None, **kernel_kwargs)[source]#

Constructs a scalar vector source from exact samples or a kernel.

Unlike the usual constructor, this method builds the evaluation function from dataset. Sample weights sum to one after normalization; omitted weights give equal mass to every sample. With kernel=None, evaluation returns the total weight of samples exactly matching each query, and zero elsewhere. With a kernel, it returns the weighted sum of its query-to-sample values. For example, pass gaussian_kernel() with bandwidth to obtain a Gaussian density estimate; no kernel is selected automatically.

All dataset columns are continuous inputs in their given order, with n_sites == dataset.shape[1] and in_dim=None. The returned source has scalar responses, with out_shape=().

Parameters

  • dataset (torch.Tensor) – Continuous coordinates with shape (n_samples, n_sites).

  • weights (torch.Tensor, optional) – Non-negative weights normalized to total mass one.

  • kernel (callable, optional) – Receives (coordinates, dataset, **kernel_kwargs) and returns (batch, n_samples) values. None uses exact coordinate matches.

  • **kernel_kwargs – Parameters owned by the selected kernel, such as bandwidth.

Returns

Scalar vector source evaluating exact masses or kernel estimates.

Return type

CallableSource

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.CallableSource.from_data(
...     torch.tensor([[0.1], [0.4], [0.1]]))
>>> source.evaluate(tk.decompositions.ConfigurationBatch(
...     torch.tensor([[0.1], [0.3]]), kind='features'))
tensor([0.6667, 0.0000])

A Gaussian kernel smooths the samples into a continuous density:

>>> source = tk.decompositions.CallableSource.from_data(
...     torch.tensor([[0.], [0.]]),
...     kernel=tk.decompositions.gaussian_kernel, bandwidth=1.)
>>> source.evaluate(tk.decompositions.ConfigurationBatch(
...     torch.tensor([[0.], [1.]]), kind='features'))
tensor([0.3989, 0.2420])
property in_dim#

Dimensions of all vector variables or paired matrix input axes.

property out_shape#

Declared or inferred function output shape.

property dtype#

Declared or inferred function output dtype.

property device#

Device on which evaluations are performed.

evaluate(configurations)[source]#

Evaluates configurations using the source’s input convention.

Parameters

configurations (ConfigurationBatch) – Inputs in in_sites order: continuous features with shape (batch, len(in_sites), *feature_shape) for CallableSource, or integer indices with shape (batch, len(in_sites)) for CallableTensorSource and its Quantics subclass. Heterogeneous continuous inputs may instead use len(in_sites) tensors.

Returns

Values with shape (batch, *out_shape), preserving input order and autograd. batch_size bounds each callable invocation.

Return type

torch.Tensor

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.CallableTensorSource(function, in_dim, **kwargs)[source]#

Finite tensor whose values are evaluated by a callable.

in_dim gives the dimension of every tensor axis, so n_sites == len(in_dim). By default, all axes are inputs and the callable returns one scalar per configuration.

Use in_sites to select only some axes as inputs. The callable receives integer indices with shape (batch, len(in_sites)), in that order, and returns the remaining axes in their original tensor order. Its output has shape (batch, *out_shape), where out_shape is determined by the dimensions of the unselected axes.

Values are computed on demand. contract_dense() evaluates all input configurations to construct the full tensor. Dtype, device and callable batching follow CallableSource; dtype can be inferred on the first evaluation.

Use matrix() to pair each input axis with an output axis. from_data() instead constructs the callable from discrete samples, using exact matches or a user-supplied kernel.

Parameters

  • function (callable) – Receives integer indices with shape (batch, len(in_sites)), in in_sites order, and returns shape (batch, *out_shape).

  • in_dim (sequence of int) – Dimensions of all represented vector axes.

  • in_sites (sequence of int, optional) – Ordered input variables. Defaults to every axis. The callable returns the complementary axes in their represented order.

  • **kwargs – Output shape, dtype, device and batching options of CallableSource.

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.CallableTensorSource(
...     lambda indices: indices.sum(-1).float(), in_dim=(2, 3))
>>> source.contract_dense()
tensor([[0., 1., 2.],
        [1., 2., 3.]])
classmethod matrix(function, in_dim, out_dim, **kwargs)[source]#

Constructs a matrix source from a callable on discrete input indices.

in_dim and out_dim must have equal lengths, with one pair per site. evaluate() receives indices with shape (batch, n_sites) in site order and returns all output axes, with out_shape == out_dim. contract_dense() returns interleaved input/output axes.

Parameters

  • function (callable) – Receives input indices and returns shape (batch, *out_dim).

  • in_dim (sequence of int) – Input and output dimensions, respectively, for each matrix site.

  • out_dim (sequence of int) – Input and output dimensions, respectively, for each matrix site.

  • **kwargs – dtype, device and batch_size options of CallableSource.

Returns

Matrix source with out_shape == out_dim.

Return type

CallableTensorSource

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.CallableTensorSource.matrix(
...     lambda indices: torch.nn.functional.one_hot(
...         indices[:, 0], num_classes=2).float(),
...     in_dim=(2,), out_dim=(2,))
>>> source.contract_dense()
tensor([[1., 0.],
        [0., 1.]])
classmethod from_data(dataset, in_dim=None, weights=None, *, kernel=None, **kernel_kwargs)[source]#

Constructs a scalar tensor source from discrete samples or a kernel.

With kernel=None, evaluation returns the total normalized weight of samples matching each query, and zero elsewhere. With a kernel, evaluation returns the weighted sum of its query-to-sample values. Both cases use all dataset columns as inputs in their given order and return scalar responses, with out_shape=().

Parameters

  • dataset (torch.Tensor) – Integer indices with shape (n_samples, n_sites).

  • in_dim (sequence of int, optional) – Dimension of each discrete input axis, in dataset column order. Inferred from observed indices when omitted without a kernel; required when a kernel is supplied.

  • weights (torch.Tensor, optional) – Non-negative weights normalized to total mass one.

  • kernel (callable, optional) – Receives (indices, dataset, **kernel_kwargs) and returns (batch, n_samples) values. None uses exact index matches.

  • **kernel_kwargs – Parameters owned by the selected kernel, such as bandwidth.

Returns

Scalar tensor source evaluating kernel estimates or exact masses.

Return type

CallableTensorSource

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.CallableTensorSource.from_data(
...     torch.tensor([[0], [2], [0]]), in_dim=(3,))
>>> source.contract_dense()
tensor([0.6667, 0.0000, 0.3333])
class tensorkrowch.decompositions.CallableQuanticsSource(function, n_coordinates, base=None, level=None, domain=None, grid_coordinates=None, *, layout=None, coordinate_map=None, **kwargs)[source]#

Coordinate callable evaluated through a finite Quantics discretization.

evaluate() receives integer digits with shape (batch, len(in_sites)) in QuantizedLayout order. The layout decodes each row into grid indices, and CoordinateMap converts these indices to domain coordinates for function.

The callable returns shape (batch, *out_shape). Each input digit is a site; any response axes are additional output sites. out_shape can be declared or inferred on first evaluation. The function is evaluated directly at grid coordinates, without interpolation. Dtype, device and batching follow CallableTensorSource.

The usual constructor accepts three ways to define the discretization: pass base, level and domain for a uniform grid with left grid points; replace domain with grid_coordinates for explicit positions; or pass an existing layout and coordinate_map together, without shorthand arguments. Shorthand layouts use ordering="interleaved" and digit_order="coarse_to_fine". Each coordinate has base ** level grid points; explicit grid sizes must match exactly.

Use matrix() for a scalar function of input and output coordinates with independent discretizations on both sides. from_data() instead quantizes a dataset and constructs its empirical vector distribution, optionally smoothed by a kernel. contract_dense() retains digit axes; contract_dense_grid_axes() combines them into one axis per coordinate.

Parameters

  • function (callable) – Receives domain coordinates of shape (batch, n_coordinates) and returns one scalar or fixed-shape tensor per configuration.

  • n_coordinates (int) – Number of domain coordinates.

  • base (int or sequence of int, optional) – Digit base and level for each coordinate. An integer applies to all coordinates; a sequence has n_coordinates entries and allows different values per coordinate. Required with the domain/grid shorthand.

  • level (int or sequence of int, optional) – Digit base and level for each coordinate. An integer applies to all coordinates; a sequence has n_coordinates entries and allows different values per coordinate. Required with the domain/grid shorthand.

  • domain (pair, sequence of pairs or torch.Tensor, optional) – Domain intervals for an affine map with left grid points. One pair applies to all coordinates; a sequence of n_coordinates pairs specifies a different interval for each coordinate. A tensor has shape (2,) or (n_coordinates, 2), respectively.

  • grid_coordinates (torch.Tensor or sequence of torch.Tensor, optional) – Explicit grid positions instead of domain, with one vector per coordinate. A sequence of n_coordinates vectors allows different grid sizes; a matrix stores one coordinate per row. A single vector defines a one-coordinate grid.

  • layout (QuantizedLayout, optional) – Digit schedule, supplied together with coordinate_map.

  • coordinate_map (CoordinateMap, optional) – Grid mapping, supplied together with layout.

  • **kwargs – out_shape, dtype, device and batch_size options of CallableSource. Response axes are appended after input digits.

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.CallableQuanticsSource(
...     lambda coordinates: torch.exp(coordinates.sum(-1)),
...     1, base=2, level=2, domain=(0., 1.))
>>> source.evaluate(tk.decompositions.ConfigurationBatch(
...     torch.tensor([[0, 0], [1, 0]])))
tensor([1.0000, 1.6487])
>>> source.contract_dense_grid_axes()
tensor([1.0000, 1.2840, 1.6487, 2.1170])
classmethod matrix(function, in_n_coordinates, out_n_coordinates, **kwargs)[source]#

Constructs a matrix source with independent input/output grids.

Unlike the usual constructor, function receives two coordinate tensors, one for each side, and returns a scalar for each paired row. Each side uses the same construction options as the usual constructor, prefixed with in_ or out_. For example, in_base, in_level and in_domain define the input grid, while out_layout and out_coordinate_map can define the output grid explicitly.

Both layouts must have the same number of digit sites, although their coordinate counts and local dimensions can differ. evaluate() receives input digits of shape (batch, n_sites) in input layout order and evaluates the callable at every output grid configuration. Each site pairs an input digit with an output digit. The returned shape is (batch, *out_dim), with out_shape == out_dim. contract_dense() interleaves input and output digit axes; contract_dense_grid_axes() groups input coordinate axes before output coordinate axes.

Parameters

  • function (callable) – Receives two tensors of shape (batch, in_n_coordinates) and (batch, out_n_coordinates), and returns shape (batch,).

  • in_n_coordinates (int) – Coordinate counts on each side.

  • out_n_coordinates (int) – Coordinate counts on each side.

  • **kwargs – in_/out_ prefixed base, level, domain, grid_coordinates, layout and coordinate_map options, plus shared dtype, device and batch_size options.

Returns

Matrix source with equal numbers of paired digit sites.

Return type

CallableQuanticsSource

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.CallableQuanticsSource.matrix(
...     lambda x, y: (x + y).sum(-1), 1, 1,
...     in_base=2, in_level=1, in_domain=(0., 1.),
...     out_base=2, out_level=1, out_domain=(0., 1.))
>>> source.evaluate(tk.decompositions.ConfigurationBatch(
...     torch.tensor([[1]])))
tensor([[0.5000, 1.0000]])
>>> source.contract_dense_grid_axes()
tensor([[0.0000, 0.5000],
        [0.5000, 1.0000]])
classmethod from_data(dataset, n_coordinates, weights=None, *, kernel=None, **kwargs)[source]#

Discretizes samples before constructing their empirical vector tensor.

Pass the same discretization options as in the usual constructor. The coordinate map assigns each dataset row to a grid index before accumulating its normalized weight. Samples mapped to the same grid point contribute to the same mass. Without a kernel, evaluation returns that mass or zero at unobserved grid points.

With kernel, each dataset row is replaced by its grid coordinates, preserving row order, duplicates and normalized weights. The kernel is evaluated against these coordinates without renormalizing its values over the grid. Additional keyword arguments, such as bandwidth, are passed to the kernel. Both cases construct vector sources with out_shape=(); this constructor does not create matrix sources.

Parameters

  • dataset (torch.Tensor) – Domain coordinates of shape (n_samples, n_coordinates).

  • n_coordinates (int) – Coordinate count, consistent with the dataset.

  • weights (torch.Tensor, optional) – Non-negative sample weights, normalized to total mass one.

  • kernel (callable, optional) – Receives query coordinates and the discretized dataset, and returns shape (batch, n_samples). None returns exact empirical masses.

  • **kwargs – Quantization arguments as in the constructor, and kernel parameters such as bandwidth for gaussian_kernel().

Returns

Discretized empirical masses or kernel estimates.

Return type

CallableQuanticsSource

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.CallableQuanticsSource.from_data(
...     torch.tensor([[0.], [0.], [0.5]]), 1,
...     base=2, level=1, domain=(0., 1.))
>>> source.contract_dense_grid_axes()
tensor([0.6667, 0.3333])

Kernel estimates use the discretized samples as centers:

>>> source = tk.decompositions.CallableQuanticsSource.from_data(
...     torch.tensor([[0.1], [0.2]]), 1,
...     base=2, level=1, domain=(0., 1.),
...     kernel=tk.decompositions.gaussian_kernel, bandwidth=1.)
>>> source.contract_dense_grid_axes()
tensor([0.3989, 0.3521])
property out_shape#

Declared or inferred function output shape.

contract_dense_grid_axes()[source]#

Materializes the same tensor with one axis per original grid coordinate.

Returns

Coordinate grid axes followed by function response axes. For a matrix, all input coordinate axes precede output coordinate axes.

Return type

torch.Tensor

tensorkrowch.decompositions.as_tensor_source(source)[source]#

Wraps a tensor or format, retaining an existing source unchanged.

A torch.Tensor is wrapped in DenseTensorSource, and a TensorFormat1D, MPS or MPO in FormatSource; these sources obtain dimensions and evaluation rules from the supplied object. An existing BaseSource is returned unchanged. Raw callables are not accepted: construct a callable source explicitly to define its sites and whether it takes discrete indices or continuous coordinates.

Parameters

source (BaseSource, TensorFormat1D, MPS, MPO or torch.Tensor) – Object providing the values to decompose.

Returns

Source carrying its own shape, dtype, device and evaluation rules.

Return type

BaseSource

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.as_tensor_source(torch.arange(4.).reshape(2, 2))
>>> source.contract_dense()
tensor([[0., 1.],
        [2., 3.]])
tensorkrowch.decompositions.gaussian_kernel(coordinates, centers, bandwidth=1.0)[source]#

Evaluates normalized Gaussian kernels centered at centers.

Each center contributes a density \(K_h(x,z)=\exp(-\frac12\sum_i((x_i-z_i)/h_i)^2) / ((2\pi)^{d/2}\prod_i h_i)\), where \(x\) is a row of coordinates, \(z\) is a row of centers, \(h_i\) is the bandwidth for coordinate \(i\), and \(d\) is n_coordinates. Scalar bandwidth is shared across coordinates. Normalization is over the full continuous domain; restricting evaluation to a finite grid does not renormalize these densities.

Parameters

  • coordinates (torch.Tensor) – Queries with shape (batch, n_coordinates).

  • centers (torch.Tensor) – Kernel centers with shape (n_centers, n_coordinates).

  • bandwidth (float, sequence[float] or torch.Tensor) – Positive finite width, either scalar or one value per coordinate. Its default is 1.0; it is not inferred from centers.

Returns

Kernel values of shape (batch, n_centers). Weights and reductions are applied by the caller. Query and parameter gradients remain.

Return type

torch.Tensor

Examples

>>> tk.decompositions.gaussian_kernel(
...     torch.tensor([[0.], [1.]]), torch.tensor([[0.]]))
tensor([[0.3989],
        [0.2420]])

SVD engines and functions#

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.TTSVD(source, *, out_device='cpu')[source]#

Decomposes a fixed dense tensor into a tensor train.

The tensor and its batch dimensions are fixed when this object is created. fit() can then be called repeatedly with different truncation criteria. Each fit is independent and returns a lightweight TTDecomposition.

The numerical sweep follows the TT-SVD algorithm introduced by I. V. Oseledets in Tensor-Train Decomposition (2011), paper.

source defines the input’s dimensions, evaluation rules and matrix grouping. Finite sources include DenseTensorSource, SparseTensorSource, FormatSource, CallableTensorSource and CallableQuanticsSource. SVD materializes their complete tensor once. A torch.Tensor is accepted directly, as is a non-Quantics TT/TR format or its matrix version. Wrap an MPS in FormatSource first.

To declare matrix inputs, use matrix() or the corresponding .matrix(...) constructor of SparseTensorSource, CallableTensorSource or CallableQuanticsSource. FormatSource instead infers matrix grouping from a matrix format. The source selects the result family and retains any Quantics layouts and coordinate maps.

Parameters

  • source (BaseSource, TensorFormat1D or torch.Tensor) – Finite tensor input, with shape and evaluation defined by the source.

  • out_device (str or torch.device, optional) – Device where finalized cores are stored. The default is "cpu". If None, cores remain on the tensor’s device.

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.DenseTensorSource(torch.ones(2, 2, 2))
>>> result = tk.decompositions.TTSVD(source).fit(rank=1)
>>> result.rank
[1, 1]
fit(rank=None, cutoff=None, atol=None, rtol=None, cum_percentage=None, renormalize=False, collect_metrics=False, verbose=0)[source]#

Runs TT-SVD with a shared truncation policy at every cut.

The active exact SVD backend is selected through tensorkrowch.set_svd_method() or tensorkrowch.svd_method(). When metrics are collected, local discarded energies and their accumulated absolute and relative reconstruction errors are returned in result.metrics.

If several truncation criteria are specified, each one provides an upper bound for the selected rank and the most restrictive bound is used. At least one singular value is always retained. The same criteria are applied at every TT cut.

The fixed tensor should have shape (*batch_shape, d_1, ..., d_n), where the first n_batches axes are optional batch dimensions and each remaining axis is the input dimension of one TT site. Thus, the desired number and input dimensions of the cores are specified directly by the non-batch shape of the tensor; reshape the tensor before constructing TTSVD if a different site factorization is required.

For more than one site, the returned cores have shapes (*batch_shape, d_1, rank_1), (*batch_shape, rank_{k-1}, d_k, rank_k) at interior sites, and (*batch_shape, rank_{n-1}, d_n) at the last site. A one-site tensor is returned as a single core with its original shape. Consequently, the result always represents an open-boundary TT.

Parameters

  • rank (int, optional) – Maximum rank allowed at every link. At each SVD cut, at most this many singular values are retained.

  • cutoff (float, optional) – Minimum singular value to keep. It must be finite and non-negative. Singular values <= cutoff are removed.

  • atol (float, optional) – Absolute tolerance over the tail sum of squared singular values. Starting from the smallest singular value, values are discarded while the accumulated sum of squares is <= atol. It must be finite and non-negative.

  • rtol (float, optional) – Relative tolerance over the tail sum of squared singular values. Starting from the smallest singular value, values are discarded while the tail sum of squares divided by the total sum of squares is <= rtol. It must be finite and in [0, 1].

  • cum_percentage (float, optional) –

    Minimum fraction of squared singular-value mass to keep. Equivalent to setting rtol = 1 - cum_percentage. It must be finite and in [0, 1].

    \[\frac{\sum_{i \in \{kept\}}{s_i^2}} {\sum_{i \in \{all\}}{s_i^2}} \ge cum\_percentage\]

  • renormalize (bool) – If True, normalizes the residual before every SVD and accumulates the extracted scale logarithmically. The complete scale is evenly redistributed over the final cores. Absolute truncation criteria and reported errors remain expressed in the scale of the original tensor.

  • collect_metrics (bool) – If True, collects local truncation records, accumulated errors and synchronized timings in result.metrics. The default is False to avoid diagnostic norm reductions, records and device synchronizations. Metrics are always collected when console output is requested.

  • verbose (bool or int) –

    Console verbosity level:

    • 0 or False: no console output;

    • 1 or True: phase title, input configuration, cut progress and final summary;

    • 2: detailed per-cut rank, error and timing information;

    • 3: level 2 output followed by every final core.

Returns

Lightweight result containing cores and ranks. Its structured metrics are empty unless collect_metrics=True or verbose>0.

Return type

TTDecomposition

Examples

Fix a tensor once and compare decompositions with different maximum ranks:

>>> tensor = torch.arange(24.).reshape(2, 3, 4)
>>> decomposer = tk.decompositions.TTSVD(tensor)
>>> rank_one = decomposer.fit(rank=1)
>>> rank_two = decomposer.fit(rank=2, collect_metrics=True)
>>> rank_one.rank
[1, 1]
>>> rank_two.rank
[2, 2]
>>> len(rank_two.metrics.truncations)
2
class tensorkrowch.decompositions.TRSVD(source, center=None, *, out_device='cpu')[source]#

Decomposes a fixed dense tensor into a tensor ring.

The tensor and a preferred interior cut are fixed when this object is created. fit() can then be called repeatedly with different truncation criteria, centers and rank policies. Each fit is independent and returns a lightweight TRDecomposition.

The algorithm first reshapes the tensor across an interior bipartition and computes one SVD. Its selected rank is represented as the product of the cyclic rank and the rank crossing the interior cut. The two resulting blocks are then decomposed by the shared TT-SVD engine while preserving those boundary ranks. No batch dimensions are supported.

This construction is based on TR-SVD by Q. Zhao et al. in Tensor Ring Decomposition (2016), paper. The implementation uses an interior bipartition followed by two TT-SVD subchains, rather than the one-direction sequence in the original algorithm.

source defines the input’s dimensions, evaluation rules and matrix grouping. Finite sources include DenseTensorSource, SparseTensorSource, FormatSource, CallableTensorSource and CallableQuanticsSource. SVD materializes their complete tensor once. A torch.Tensor is accepted directly, as is a non-Quantics TT/TR format or its matrix version. Wrap an MPS in FormatSource first.

To declare matrix inputs, use matrix() or the corresponding .matrix(...) constructor of SparseTensorSource, CallableTensorSource or CallableQuanticsSource. FormatSource instead infers matrix grouping from a matrix format. The source selects the result family and retains any Quantics layouts and coordinate maps.

Parameters

  • source (BaseSource, TensorFormat1D or torch.Tensor) – Finite tensor input, with shape and evaluation defined by the source.

  • center (int, optional) – Interior cut between sites center - 1 and center. It should satisfy 1 <= center < tensor.ndim. The default is the middle cut.

  • out_device (str or torch.device, optional) – Device where finalized cores are stored. The default is "cpu". If None, cores remain on the tensor’s device.

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.DenseTensorSource(torch.ones(2, 2, 2))
>>> result = tk.decompositions.TRSVD(source).fit(rank=1)
>>> result.rank
[1, 1, 1]
fit(center=None, rank=None, cutoff=None, atol=None, rtol=None, cum_percentage=None, renormalize=False, collect_metrics=False, verbose=0)[source]#

Runs TR-SVD from an interior bipartition of the fixed tensor.

The active exact SVD backend is selected through tensorkrowch.set_svd_method() or tensorkrowch.svd_method(). When metrics are collected, discarded energies are returned as phase-labelled local diagnostics. They are not combined into a global reconstruction bound because the successive TR-SVD truncations are not all orthogonal in one common scale.

If rank is an integer, it is a shared upper bound for every TR rank and its square bounds the initial bipartition. Local truncation criteria may therefore select a different effective rank at each site. With None, ranks are discovered from the selected SVD dimensions. The selected rank is split with the smallest admissible product and the most balanced pair breaks ties. Any extra capacity required by the cap is padded only with structural zeros and recorded in result.metadata.

Here, initial_rank is the rank actually selected by the initial SVD, whereas initial_capacity is the product of the two TR ranks used to represent it. Their difference is initial_padding. For example, an initial_rank of 7 may use ranks 2 and 4, giving an initial_capacity of 8 and an initial_padding of 1.

The fixed tensor should have shape (d_1, ..., d_n), with one input dimension per TR site. The returned cores all have shape (rank_{k-1}, d_k, rank_k), where the left rank of the first core matches the right rank of the last core. Consequently, the result always represents a cyclic TR.

Parameters

  • center (int, optional) – Interior cut used for this fit. If omitted, the center fixed at construction is used.

  • rank (int, optional) – Maximum rank allowed at every link. At each subchain SVD cut, at most this many singular values are retained. The initial bipartition retains at most rank ** 2 singular values before its selected rank is factorized into two TR ranks.

  • cutoff (float, optional) – Minimum singular value to keep. It must be finite and non-negative. Singular values <= cutoff are removed.

  • atol (float, optional) – Absolute tolerance over the tail sum of squared singular values. Starting from the smallest singular value, values are discarded while the accumulated sum of squares is <= atol. It must be finite and non-negative.

  • rtol (float, optional) – Relative tolerance over the tail sum of squared singular values. Starting from the smallest singular value, values are discarded while the tail sum of squares divided by the total sum of squares is <= rtol. It must be finite and in [0, 1].

  • cum_percentage (float, optional) –

    Minimum fraction of squared singular-value mass to keep. Equivalent to setting rtol = 1 - cum_percentage. It must be finite and in [0, 1].

    \[\]

  • ge (frac{sum_{i in {kept}}{s_i^2}}{sum_{i in {all}}{s_i^2}}) – cum_percentage

  • renormalize (bool) – If True, normalizes the residual before every SVD and accumulates extracted scales logarithmically. Complete scales are redistributed without changing the represented tensor.

  • collect_metrics (bool) – If True, collects phase-labelled local truncation records and synchronized timings in result.metrics. The default is False to avoid diagnostic norm reductions, records and device synchronizations. Metrics are always collected when console output is requested.

  • verbose (bool or int) –

    Console verbosity level:

    • 0 or False: no console output;

    • 1 or True: phase title, input configuration, cut progress and final summary;

    • 2: detailed per-cut rank, error and timing information;

    • 3: level 2 output followed by every final core.

Returns

Lightweight result containing cores and ranks. Its structured metrics are empty unless collect_metrics=True or verbose>0.

Return type

TRDecomposition

Examples

Fix a tensor and compare shared rank caps at the middle cut:

>>> tensor = torch.arange(16.).reshape(2, 2, 2, 2)
>>> decomposer = tk.decompositions.TRSVD(tensor)
>>> rank_one = decomposer.fit(rank=1)
>>> rank_two = decomposer.fit(rank=2)
>>> max(rank_one.rank)
1
>>> max(rank_two.rank) <= 2
True
class tensorkrowch.decompositions.TTMSVD(source, *, out_device='cpu')[source]#

Decomposes a matrix source using the shared TT-SVD algorithm.

The source owns paired dimensions and axis ordering. Input/output pairs are fused for the numerical sweep and restored in the returned matrix decomposition. Quantics source metadata selects a Quantics result.

source defines the input’s dimensions, evaluation rules and matrix grouping. Finite sources include DenseTensorSource, SparseTensorSource, FormatSource, CallableTensorSource and CallableQuanticsSource. SVD materializes their complete tensor once. A torch.Tensor is accepted directly, as is a non-Quantics TT/TR format or its matrix version. Wrap an MPS in FormatSource first.

To declare matrix inputs, use matrix() or the corresponding .matrix(...) constructor of SparseTensorSource, CallableTensorSource or CallableQuanticsSource. FormatSource instead infers matrix grouping from a matrix format. The source selects the result family and retains any Quantics layouts and coordinate maps.

Tensors passed directly use grouped axes (in_0, in_1, ..., out_0, out_1, ...). For interleaved input axes, construct DenseTensorSource.matrix(tensor, ordering="interleaved") explicitly. The source supplies interleaved axes to the numerical algorithm in both cases.

Parameters

  • source (BaseSource or torch.Tensor) – Finite matrix source declaring paired dimensions, or a tensor with grouped input/output axes. Wrap matrix formats in FormatSource.

  • out_device (str or torch.device, optional) – Device for finalized cores. None retains the evaluation device.

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.DenseTensorSource.matrix(
...     torch.eye(4).reshape(2, 2, 2, 2))
>>> result = tk.decompositions.TTMSVD(source).fit(rank=2)
>>> result.in_dim
(2, 2)
fit(rank=None, cutoff=None, atol=None, rtol=None, cum_percentage=None, renormalize=False, collect_metrics=False, verbose=0)#

Runs TT-SVD with a shared truncation policy at every cut.

The active exact SVD backend is selected through tensorkrowch.set_svd_method() or tensorkrowch.svd_method(). When metrics are collected, local discarded energies and their accumulated absolute and relative reconstruction errors are returned in result.metrics.

If several truncation criteria are specified, each one provides an upper bound for the selected rank and the most restrictive bound is used. At least one singular value is always retained. The same criteria are applied at every TT cut.

The fixed tensor should have shape (*batch_shape, d_1, ..., d_n), where the first n_batches axes are optional batch dimensions and each remaining axis is the input dimension of one TT site. Thus, the desired number and input dimensions of the cores are specified directly by the non-batch shape of the tensor; reshape the tensor before constructing TTSVD if a different site factorization is required.

For more than one site, the returned cores have shapes (*batch_shape, d_1, rank_1), (*batch_shape, rank_{k-1}, d_k, rank_k) at interior sites, and (*batch_shape, rank_{n-1}, d_n) at the last site. A one-site tensor is returned as a single core with its original shape. Consequently, the result always represents an open-boundary TT.

Parameters

  • rank (int, optional) – Maximum rank allowed at every link. At each SVD cut, at most this many singular values are retained.

  • cutoff (float, optional) – Minimum singular value to keep. It must be finite and non-negative. Singular values <= cutoff are removed.

  • atol (float, optional) – Absolute tolerance over the tail sum of squared singular values. Starting from the smallest singular value, values are discarded while the accumulated sum of squares is <= atol. It must be finite and non-negative.

  • rtol (float, optional) – Relative tolerance over the tail sum of squared singular values. Starting from the smallest singular value, values are discarded while the tail sum of squares divided by the total sum of squares is <= rtol. It must be finite and in [0, 1].

  • cum_percentage (float, optional) –

    Minimum fraction of squared singular-value mass to keep. Equivalent to setting rtol = 1 - cum_percentage. It must be finite and in [0, 1].

    \[\frac{\sum_{i \in \{kept\}}{s_i^2}} {\sum_{i \in \{all\}}{s_i^2}} \ge cum\_percentage\]

  • renormalize (bool) – If True, normalizes the residual before every SVD and accumulates the extracted scale logarithmically. The complete scale is evenly redistributed over the final cores. Absolute truncation criteria and reported errors remain expressed in the scale of the original tensor.

  • collect_metrics (bool) – If True, collects local truncation records, accumulated errors and synchronized timings in result.metrics. The default is False to avoid diagnostic norm reductions, records and device synchronizations. Metrics are always collected when console output is requested.

  • verbose (bool or int) –

    Console verbosity level:

    • 0 or False: no console output;

    • 1 or True: phase title, input configuration, cut progress and final summary;

    • 2: detailed per-cut rank, error and timing information;

    • 3: level 2 output followed by every final core.

Returns

Lightweight result containing cores and ranks. Its structured metrics are empty unless collect_metrics=True or verbose>0.

Return type

TTDecomposition

Examples

Fix a tensor once and compare decompositions with different maximum ranks:

>>> tensor = torch.arange(24.).reshape(2, 3, 4)
>>> decomposer = tk.decompositions.TTSVD(tensor)
>>> rank_one = decomposer.fit(rank=1)
>>> rank_two = decomposer.fit(rank=2, collect_metrics=True)
>>> rank_one.rank
[1, 1]
>>> rank_two.rank
[2, 2]
>>> len(rank_two.metrics.truncations)
2
class tensorkrowch.decompositions.TRMSVD(source, center=None, *, out_device='cpu')[source]#

Decomposes a matrix source using the shared TR-SVD algorithm.

The source owns paired dimensions and axis ordering. Input/output pairs are fused for the numerical sweep and restored in the returned matrix decomposition. Quantics source metadata selects a Quantics result.

source defines the input’s dimensions, evaluation rules and matrix grouping. Finite sources include DenseTensorSource, SparseTensorSource, FormatSource, CallableTensorSource and CallableQuanticsSource. SVD materializes their complete tensor once. A torch.Tensor is accepted directly, as is a non-Quantics TT/TR format or its matrix version. Wrap an MPS in FormatSource first.

To declare matrix inputs, use matrix() or the corresponding .matrix(...) constructor of SparseTensorSource, CallableTensorSource or CallableQuanticsSource. FormatSource instead infers matrix grouping from a matrix format. The source selects the result family and retains any Quantics layouts and coordinate maps.

Tensors passed directly use grouped axes (in_0, in_1, ..., out_0, out_1, ...). For interleaved input axes, construct DenseTensorSource.matrix(tensor, ordering="interleaved") explicitly. The source supplies interleaved axes to the numerical algorithm in both cases.

Parameters

  • source (BaseSource or torch.Tensor) – Finite matrix source declaring paired dimensions, or a tensor with grouped input/output axes. Wrap matrix formats in FormatSource.

  • center (int, optional) – Preferred interior cut, passed to TRSVD.

  • out_device (str or torch.device, optional) – Device for finalized cores. None retains the evaluation device.

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.DenseTensorSource.matrix(
...     torch.eye(4).reshape(2, 2, 2, 2))
>>> result = tk.decompositions.TRMSVD(source).fit(rank=2)
>>> result.in_dim
(2, 2)
fit(center=None, rank=None, cutoff=None, atol=None, rtol=None, cum_percentage=None, renormalize=False, collect_metrics=False, verbose=0)#

Runs TR-SVD from an interior bipartition of the fixed tensor.

The active exact SVD backend is selected through tensorkrowch.set_svd_method() or tensorkrowch.svd_method(). When metrics are collected, discarded energies are returned as phase-labelled local diagnostics. They are not combined into a global reconstruction bound because the successive TR-SVD truncations are not all orthogonal in one common scale.

If rank is an integer, it is a shared upper bound for every TR rank and its square bounds the initial bipartition. Local truncation criteria may therefore select a different effective rank at each site. With None, ranks are discovered from the selected SVD dimensions. The selected rank is split with the smallest admissible product and the most balanced pair breaks ties. Any extra capacity required by the cap is padded only with structural zeros and recorded in result.metadata.

Here, initial_rank is the rank actually selected by the initial SVD, whereas initial_capacity is the product of the two TR ranks used to represent it. Their difference is initial_padding. For example, an initial_rank of 7 may use ranks 2 and 4, giving an initial_capacity of 8 and an initial_padding of 1.

The fixed tensor should have shape (d_1, ..., d_n), with one input dimension per TR site. The returned cores all have shape (rank_{k-1}, d_k, rank_k), where the left rank of the first core matches the right rank of the last core. Consequently, the result always represents a cyclic TR.

Parameters

  • center (int, optional) – Interior cut used for this fit. If omitted, the center fixed at construction is used.

  • rank (int, optional) – Maximum rank allowed at every link. At each subchain SVD cut, at most this many singular values are retained. The initial bipartition retains at most rank ** 2 singular values before its selected rank is factorized into two TR ranks.

  • cutoff (float, optional) – Minimum singular value to keep. It must be finite and non-negative. Singular values <= cutoff are removed.

  • atol (float, optional) – Absolute tolerance over the tail sum of squared singular values. Starting from the smallest singular value, values are discarded while the accumulated sum of squares is <= atol. It must be finite and non-negative.

  • rtol (float, optional) – Relative tolerance over the tail sum of squared singular values. Starting from the smallest singular value, values are discarded while the tail sum of squares divided by the total sum of squares is <= rtol. It must be finite and in [0, 1].

  • cum_percentage (float, optional) –

    Minimum fraction of squared singular-value mass to keep. Equivalent to setting rtol = 1 - cum_percentage. It must be finite and in [0, 1].

    \[\]

  • ge (frac{sum_{i in {kept}}{s_i^2}}{sum_{i in {all}}{s_i^2}}) – cum_percentage

  • renormalize (bool) – If True, normalizes the residual before every SVD and accumulates extracted scales logarithmically. Complete scales are redistributed without changing the represented tensor.

  • collect_metrics (bool) – If True, collects phase-labelled local truncation records and synchronized timings in result.metrics. The default is False to avoid diagnostic norm reductions, records and device synchronizations. Metrics are always collected when console output is requested.

  • verbose (bool or int) –

    Console verbosity level:

    • 0 or False: no console output;

    • 1 or True: phase title, input configuration, cut progress and final summary;

    • 2: detailed per-cut rank, error and timing information;

    • 3: level 2 output followed by every final core.

Returns

Lightweight result containing cores and ranks. Its structured metrics are empty unless collect_metrics=True or verbose>0.

Return type

TRDecomposition

Examples

Fix a tensor and compare shared rank caps at the middle cut:

>>> tensor = torch.arange(16.).reshape(2, 2, 2, 2)
>>> decomposer = tk.decompositions.TRSVD(tensor)
>>> rank_one = decomposer.fit(rank=1)
>>> rank_two = decomposer.fit(rank=2)
>>> max(rank_one.rank)
1
>>> max(rank_two.rank) <= 2
True

Materializes the full digit tensor from source and runs TTSVD.fit() through TTSVD. The result retains the source’s layouts and coordinate maps for coordinate evaluation.

Construct CallableQuanticsSource first to define the callable, digit ordering and coordinate grid; use matrix() for paired input/output coordinates. The source selects the vector or matrix result; this function only controls its decomposition.

  • atol (float, optional) – Absolute tolerance over the tail sum of squared singular values. Starting from the smallest singular value, values are discarded while the accumulated sum of squares is <= atol. It must be finite and non-negative.

  • cum_percentage (float, optional) – Minimum fraction of squared singular-value mass to keep. Equivalent to setting rtol = 1 - cum_percentage. It must be finite and in [0, 1].

  • renormalize (bool) – If True, normalizes the residual before every SVD, accumulates its scale logarithmically and evenly redistributes the complete scale over the final cores. Absolute criteria and reported errors preserve the scale of the original sampled tensor.

  • out_device (str or torch.device, optional) – Device where finalized cores are stored. If None, they remain on the source device. The default is "cpu".

    • 3: level 2 output followed by every final core.

    • 1 or True: phase title, input configuration, cut progress and final summary;
