    • 3: level 2 output followed by every final core.

  • collect_metrics (bool) – Whether to collect structured error, truncation and timing metrics. With False and verbose=0, diagnostic reductions and synchronized timings are skipped.

Returns

Quantics decomposition with cores, coordinate information and optional metrics.

Return type

QTRDecomposition

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.CallableQuanticsSource(
...     lambda coordinates: torch.exp(coordinates.sum(-1)),
...     n_coordinates=1, base=2, level=3, domain=(0., 1.))
>>> result = tk.decompositions.qtr_svd(source, rank=1)
>>> result.evaluate_indices(torch.tensor([[0], [4]]))
tensor([1.0000, 1.6487])
tensorkrowch.decompositions.qttm_svd(source, *, rank=None, cutoff=None, atol=None, rtol=None, cum_percentage=None, renormalize=False, out_device='cpu', verbose=0, collect_metrics=False)[source]#

Decomposes a discretized coordinate callable into QTTM cores.

Materializes the full digit tensor from source and runs TTMSVD.fit() through TTMSVD. The result retains the source’s layouts and coordinate maps for coordinate evaluation.

Construct the input with matrix() to define paired input/output coordinates, digit layouts and grids. This function controls the decomposition and retains that information.

Parameters

  • source (CallableQuanticsSource) – Callable with its digit layout and coordinate maps.

  • rank (int, optional) – Maximum rank allowed at every link. At each SVD cut, at most this many singular values are retained.

  • cutoff (float, optional) – Minimum singular value to keep. It must be finite and non-negative. Singular values <= cutoff are removed.

  • atol (float, optional) – Absolute tolerance over the tail sum of squared singular values. Starting from the smallest singular value, values are discarded while the accumulated sum of squares is <= atol. It must be finite and non-negative.

  • rtol (float, optional) – Relative tolerance over the tail sum of squared singular values. Starting from the smallest singular value, values are discarded while the tail sum of squares divided by the total sum of squares is <= rtol. It must be finite and in [0, 1].

  • cum_percentage (float, optional) – Minimum fraction of squared singular-value mass to keep. Equivalent to setting rtol = 1 - cum_percentage. It must be finite and in [0, 1].

  • renormalize (bool) – If True, normalizes the residual before every SVD, accumulates its scale logarithmically and evenly redistributes the complete scale over the final cores. Absolute criteria and reported errors preserve the scale of the original sampled tensor.

  • out_device (str or torch.device, optional) – Device where finalized cores are stored. If None, they remain on the source device. The default is "cpu".

  • verbose (bool or int) –

    Console verbosity level:

    • 0 or False: no console output;

    • 1 or True: phase title, input configuration, cut progress and final summary;

    • 2: detailed per-cut rank, error and timing information;

    • 3: level 2 output followed by every final core.

  • collect_metrics (bool) – Whether to collect structured error, truncation and timing metrics. With False and verbose=0, diagnostic reductions and synchronized timings are skipped.

Returns

Quantics decomposition with cores, coordinate information and optional metrics.

Return type

QTTMDecomposition

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.CallableQuanticsSource.matrix(
...     lambda inputs, outputs: torch.exp(
...         inputs.sum(-1) + outputs.sum(-1)),
...     in_n_coordinates=1, out_n_coordinates=1,
...     in_base=2, out_base=2, in_level=3, out_level=3,
...     in_domain=(0., 1.), out_domain=(0., 1.))
>>> result = tk.decompositions.qttm_svd(source, rank=1)
>>> result.evaluate_indices(
...     torch.tensor([[0], [4]]), torch.tensor([[0], [0]]))
tensor([1.0000, 1.6487])
tensorkrowch.decompositions.qtrm_svd(source, center=None, *, rank=None, cutoff=None, atol=None, rtol=None, cum_percentage=None, renormalize=False, out_device='cpu', verbose=0, collect_metrics=False)[source]#

Decomposes a discretized coordinate callable into QTRM cores.

Materializes the full digit tensor from source and runs TRMSVD.fit() through TRMSVD. The result retains the source’s layouts and coordinate maps for coordinate evaluation.

Construct the input with matrix() to define paired input/output coordinates, digit layouts and grids. This function controls the decomposition and retains that information.

Parameters

  • source (CallableQuanticsSource) – Callable with its digit layout and coordinate maps.

  • center (int, optional) – Interior cut from which the cyclic decomposition starts. If omitted, uses the middle of the digit chain.

  • rank (int, optional) – Maximum rank allowed at every link. At each subchain SVD cut, at most this many singular values are retained. The initial bipartition retains at most rank ** 2 singular values before its selected rank is factorized into two TRM ranks.

  • cutoff (float, optional) – Minimum singular value to keep. It must be finite and non-negative. Singular values <= cutoff are removed.

  • atol (float, optional) – Absolute tolerance over the tail sum of squared singular values. Starting from the smallest singular value, values are discarded while the accumulated sum of squares is <= atol. It must be finite and non-negative.

  • rtol (float, optional) – Relative tolerance over the tail sum of squared singular values. Starting from the smallest singular value, values are discarded while the tail sum of squares divided by the total sum of squares is <= rtol. It must be finite and in [0, 1].

  • cum_percentage (float, optional) – Minimum fraction of squared singular-value mass to keep. Equivalent to setting rtol = 1 - cum_percentage. It must be finite and in [0, 1].

  • renormalize (bool) – If True, normalizes residuals before SVDs and accumulates their scales logarithmically before redistributing them over final cores.

  • out_device (str or torch.device, optional) – Device where finalized cores are stored. If None, they remain on the source device. The default is "cpu".

  • verbose (bool or int) –

    Console verbosity level:

    • 0 or False: no console output;

    • 1 or True: phase title, input configuration, cut progress and final summary;

    • 2: detailed per-cut rank, error and timing information;

    • 3: level 2 output followed by every final core.

  • collect_metrics (bool) – Whether to collect structured error, truncation and timing metrics. With False and verbose=0, diagnostic reductions and synchronized timings are skipped.

Returns

Quantics decomposition with cores, coordinate information and optional metrics.

Return type

QTRMDecomposition

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.CallableQuanticsSource.matrix(
...     lambda inputs, outputs: torch.exp(
...         inputs.sum(-1) + outputs.sum(-1)),
...     in_n_coordinates=1, out_n_coordinates=1,
...     in_base=2, out_base=2, in_level=3, out_level=3,
...     in_domain=(0., 1.), out_domain=(0., 1.))
>>> result = tk.decompositions.qtrm_svd(source, rank=1)
>>> result.evaluate_indices(
...     torch.tensor([[0], [4]]), torch.tensor([[0], [0]]))
tensor([1.0000, 1.6487])
tensorkrowch.set_svd_method(method)[source]#

Sets the process-wide default exact SVD backend.

Parameters

method ({"svd", "qr_svd"}) – Backend used by subsequent SVD-based operations outside a temporary svd_method() context.

tensorkrowch.svd_method(method, refine=None)[source]#

Temporarily selects the exact SVD backend in the current context.

The previous backend is restored even if the context exits with an exception. Nested contexts are supported and the override is local to the current thread or asynchronous context.

Parameters

  • method ({"svd", "qr_svd"}) – Backend used inside the context.

  • refine (bool, optional) – Whether to recursively refine small singular values, independently of the backend. If omitted, inherits the active refinement setting.

Examples

>>> tensor = torch.arange(8.).reshape(2, 2, 2)
>>> with tk.svd_method('qr_svd', refine=True):
...     cores = tk.decompositions.tt_svd(tensor, rank=2).cores
...     active_settings = (tk.get_svd_method(), tk.get_svd_refinement())
>>> active_settings
('qr_svd', True)
>>> [tuple(core.shape) for core in cores]
[(2, 2), (2, 2, 2), (2, 2)]

ALS engines and policies#

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.TTALS(source, *, mask=None, weights=None, out_device='cpu')[source]#

Approximates a fixed finite tensor by one-site TT-ALS.

Construction fixes the source, its dimensions and the weighted objective. Repeated fit() calls can use different ranks, initial cores, samplers and solvers. Exact fits cache all target values on first use; sampled fits query only their selected configurations. A sparse boolean mask defines permanent observations, including observed values that are zero.

Vector, matrix and Quantics sources use the same scalar local solves; the result restores the source’s paired dimensions and coordinate metadata. Continuous inputs need discretization before ALS. Structural batches are not supported. Sweeps alternate forward and reverse; each directional pass counts once toward max_sweeps.

Parameters

  • source (BaseSource, TensorFormat1D, MPS, MPO or torch.Tensor) – Finite tensor input, with shape and evaluation defined by the source.

  • mask (BaseSource or torch.Tensor, optional) – Boolean tensor of participating entries. True participates; False is missing. A sparse mask fixes its stored true entries.

  • weights (torch.Tensor, optional) – Non-negative multiplicative residual weights with shape in_dim of the scalar problem; matrix input/output pairs are fused.

  • out_device (str or torch.device, optional) – Device where finalized cores are stored. The default is "cpu"; None keeps them on the computation device.

Examples

>>> engine = tk.decompositions.TTALS(torch.ones(2, 3))
>>> result = engine.fit(rank=1)
>>> tuple(result.contract_dense().shape)
(2, 3)
fit(rank=None, initial_cores=None, fixed_cores=None, gauge='qr', renormalize=True, sampler=None, solver=None, convergence=None, generator=None, collect_metrics=False, verbose=0)[source]#

Fits a TT by alternating one-site least-squares solves.

Sweeps alternate forward and reverse. Each directional pass counts once toward max_sweeps. Without initial_cores, initializes random cores at the requested ranks. To start from an SVD approximation, compute it separately and pass its result as initial_cores. Supplied cores are copied.

With gauge="qr", prepares right-isometric cores before the first sweep, starting at the right end of the initial trainable segment. This segment ends before the first fixed core, or at the chain’s right boundary when no cores are fixed. The contraction is preserved; fixed cores and sites beyond that segment are unchanged.

Parameters

  • rank (int or sequence of int, optional) – One upper bound per internal link, or a shared bound. Random ranks are clipped to feasible dimensions. Required without initial_cores.

  • initial_cores (TensorFormat1D or sequence of torch.Tensor, optional) – Initial approximation with matching topology, physical dimensions, dtype and device. Its ranks must respect rank when provided.

  • fixed_cores (sequence of torch.Tensor or None, optional) – One entry per site. Tensor entries replace the corresponding initial core and remain bitwise unchanged throughout ALS.

  • gauge ({"none", "qr"}) – QR moves a factor into the immediate trainable neighbor after each local solve. No factor is discarded if that receiver is unavailable.

  • renormalize (bool) – Whether cached environments remove global norms and retain their logarithmic scales. The local least-squares objective is preserved.

  • sampler (SamplingPolicy, optional) – Row-sampling configuration. None uses the full tensor or the permanent observations selected by a sparse boolean mask.

  • solver (LeastSquaresSolver, optional) – Local solver and its scaling and regularization settings. Defaults to an unregularized solver with automatic column scaling.

  • convergence (ConvergencePolicy, optional) – Complete-sweep stopping criteria and independent error-evaluation budget. Defaults to ten sweeps. Sampled fits cache fixed uniform evaluation entries and measure the current approximation on them after every sweep.

  • generator (torch.Generator, optional) – Generator used by random initialization and row sampling. Its device must match the source values.

  • collect_metrics (bool) – Whether to record local solves, complete-sweep errors and timings.

  • verbose (bool or int) – Console verbosity from 0 (silent) to 3 (most detailed).

Returns

Approximation with cores, metadata and optional metrics. Matrix and Quantics sources select the corresponding result family.

Return type

TTDecomposition

Examples

>>> tensor = torch.ones(2, 3, 2, dtype=torch.float64)
>>> result = tk.decompositions.TTALS(tensor).fit(rank=1)
>>> torch.allclose(result.contract_dense(), tensor)
True
class tensorkrowch.decompositions.TRALS(source, *, mask=None, weights=None, out_device='cpu')[source]#

Approximates a fixed finite tensor by one-site TR-ALS.

Construction fixes the source, its dimensions and the weighted objective. Repeated fit() calls can use different ranks, initial cores, samplers and solvers. Exact fits cache all target values on first use; sampled fits query only their selected configurations. A sparse boolean mask defines permanent observations, including observed values that are zero.

Vector, matrix and Quantics sources use the same scalar local solves; the result restores the source’s paired dimensions and coordinate metadata. Continuous inputs need discretization before ALS. Structural batches are not supported. Sweeps visit sites in increasing order around the ring; each complete pass counts once toward max_sweeps.

Parameters

  • source (BaseSource, TensorFormat1D, MPS, MPO or torch.Tensor) – Finite tensor input, with shape and evaluation defined by the source.

  • mask (BaseSource or torch.Tensor, optional) – Boolean tensor of participating entries. True participates; False is missing. A sparse mask fixes its stored true entries.

  • weights (torch.Tensor, optional) – Non-negative multiplicative residual weights with shape in_dim of the scalar problem; matrix input/output pairs are fused.

  • out_device (str or torch.device, optional) – Device where finalized cores are stored. The default is "cpu"; None keeps them on the computation device.

Examples

>>> engine = tk.decompositions.TRALS(torch.ones(2, 3))
>>> result = engine.fit(rank=1)
>>> tuple(result.contract_dense().shape)
(2, 3)
fit(rank=None, initial_cores=None, fixed_cores=None, gauge='qr', renormalize=True, sampler=None, solver=None, convergence=None, generator=None, collect_metrics=False, verbose=0)[source]#

Fits a TR by alternating one-site least-squares solves.

Sweeps visit sites in increasing order around the ring. Each complete pass counts once toward max_sweeps. Without initial_cores, initializes random cores at the requested ranks. To start from an SVD approximation, compute it separately and pass its result as initial_cores. Supplied cores are copied.

Parameters

  • rank (int or sequence of int, optional) – One upper bound per right link, or a shared bound. The last link closes the ring. Required without initial_cores.

  • initial_cores (TensorFormat1D or sequence of torch.Tensor, optional) – Initial approximation with matching topology, physical dimensions, dtype and device. Its ranks must respect rank when provided.

  • fixed_cores (sequence of torch.Tensor or None, optional) – One entry per site. Tensor entries replace the corresponding initial core and remain bitwise unchanged throughout ALS.

  • gauge ({"none", "qr"}) – QR moves a factor into the immediate trainable neighbor after each local solve. No factor is discarded if that receiver is unavailable.

  • renormalize (bool) – Whether cached environments remove global norms and retain their logarithmic scales. The local least-squares objective is preserved.

  • sampler (SamplingPolicy, optional) – Row-sampling configuration. None uses the full tensor or the permanent observations selected by a sparse boolean mask.

  • solver (LeastSquaresSolver, optional) – Local solver and its scaling and regularization settings. Defaults to an unregularized solver with automatic column scaling.

  • convergence (ConvergencePolicy, optional) – Complete-sweep stopping criteria and independent error-evaluation budget. Defaults to ten sweeps. Sampled fits cache fixed uniform evaluation entries and measure the current approximation on them after every sweep.

  • generator (torch.Generator, optional) – Generator used by random initialization and row sampling. Its device must match the source values.

  • collect_metrics (bool) – Whether to record local solves, complete-sweep errors and timings.

  • verbose (bool or int) – Console verbosity from 0 (silent) to 3 (most detailed).

Returns

Approximation with cores, metadata and optional metrics. Matrix and Quantics sources select the corresponding result family.

Return type

TRDecomposition

Examples

>>> tensor = torch.ones(2, 3, 2, dtype=torch.float64)
>>> result = tk.decompositions.TRALS(tensor).fit(rank=1)
>>> torch.allclose(result.contract_dense(), tensor)
True

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.ConvergencePolicy(max_sweeps=10, atol=None, rtol=None, stagnation_rtol=None, patience=None, keep_best=False, callback=None, error_samples=16384)[source]#

Defines ALS stopping rules at complete sweep boundaries.

Exact fits measure the full tensor or permanent observed entries. Sampled fits measure the complete approximation on a separate, fixed uniform set of entries. Error thresholds and best-state retention use this common measure, independently of the rows selected for local solves.

Parameters

  • max_sweeps (int) – Positive maximum number of directional sweeps. Default is 10.

  • atol (float, optional) – Stop when the absolute objective error is at most this value. For sampled evaluation, its norm is scaled to the complete tensor size.

  • rtol (float, optional) – Stop when the relative objective error is at most this value. Sampled evaluation estimates both residual and target norms on the fixed set.

  • stagnation_rtol (float, optional) – Maximum relative change between consecutive complete-sweep errors for a sweep to count as stable. These tolerances are objective tolerances, not singular-value truncation criteria.

  • patience (int, optional) – Consecutive stable sweeps required. Defaults to one when stagnation_rtol is set; otherwise it must be omitted.

  • keep_best (bool) – Restore the best complete-sweep state before returning. Default is False.

  • callback (callable, optional) – Called as callback(sweep_record, cores) after a complete sweep. Return True to stop. Cores are the current state; the callback should not mutate them or the backend caches.

  • error_samples (int, optional) – Number of fixed uniform entries used to measure sampled fits. Default is 16384. None requests exact evaluation; budgets covering the full tensor also use exact evaluation. Full and observed fits always measure their complete objective. This budget is independent of the sampler used for core updates.

Examples

>>> policy = tk.decompositions.ConvergencePolicy(max_sweeps=20, rtol=1e-8)
>>> policy.max_sweeps, policy.requires_fixed_objective
(20, True)
property requires_fixed_objective#

Whether the policy compares objective values across sweeps.

validate_objective(has_fixed_objective)[source]#

Validates that the objective supports the requested stopping rules.

Parameters

has_fixed_objective (bool) – Whether complete sweeps measure the same target entries.

stopping_reason(record, stable_sweeps)[source]#

Evaluates objective tolerances, stability and the sweep budget.

Parameters

  • record (SweepRecord) – Measurements at the end of the current directional sweep.

  • stable_sweeps (int) – Number of preceding consecutive sweeps satisfying stagnation_rtol.

Returns

Stopping reason, if any, and updated consecutive stability count.

Return type

tuple[str or None, int]

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.SamplingPolicy(n_samples, method='uniform', reuse_sweeps=1, uniform_mix=0.0)[source]#

Configures row sampling for TTALS and TRALS.

Omit the engine’s sampler argument to fit the complete tensor or its fixed observations. Uniform sampling reuses configurations across sites; leverage sampling rebuilds its distribution at each active site.

Parameters

  • n_samples (int) – Positive number of sampled configurations. TR leverage methods count environment configurations and retain the complete active input fiber, giving n_samples * in_dim[site] scalar rows per local system.

  • method ({"uniform", "leverage", "exact_leverage"}, optional) – Uniform sampling is the default. "leverage" uses exact leverage in mixed-canonical TT form and a product-leverage proposal for TR. "exact_leverage" uses the cyclic Gram construction and is TR-only.

  • reuse_sweeps (int, optional) – Number of directional sweeps sharing a uniform sample generation. Defaults to 1. Leverage methods require 1 because their distributions depend on the current cores.

  • uniform_mix (float, optional) – Uniform component mixed into a leverage proposal, in [0, 1]. Defaults to 0. Uniform sampling requires 0.

Examples

>>> sampler = tk.decompositions.SamplingPolicy(64, method='leverage')
>>> sampler.n_samples, sampler.reuse_sweeps
(64, 1)

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.LeastSquaresSolver(l2_reg=0.0, l2_reg_mode='absolute', rcond=None, column_scaling='auto', system_scaling=True, driver=None)[source]#

Solves local least-squares systems with optional Tikhonov regularization.

The solver minimizes \(\|A x - b\|_2^2 + \lambda \|x\|_2^2\). Tikhonov regularization is represented by augmented rows, never by normal equations. Column scaling is then applied as a change of variables to the complete augmented matrix, followed by one global scaling of both matrix and right-hand side.

Parameters

  • l2_reg (float, optional) – Non-negative regularization coefficient. In "absolute" mode this is lambda. In "relative" mode it is multiplied by the square of the RMS column norm of the original environment.

  • l2_reg_mode ({"absolute", "relative"}, optional) – Interpretation of l2_reg before any numerical scaling.

  • rcond (float or None, optional) – Cutoff forwarded to torch.linalg.lstsq().

  • column_scaling (bool or "auto", optional) – Whether to balance columns. "auto" activates when the ratio of non-zero column norms exceeds 1 / sqrt(machine epsilon).

  • system_scaling (bool, optional) – Whether to divide the complete transformed system by its largest magnitude before solving.

  • driver (str or None, optional) – Preferred torch.linalg.lstsq() driver. CPU failures are retried with the remaining supported drivers and the effective driver is stored in LocalSolveRecord.

Examples

>>> matrix = torch.eye(2)
>>> target = torch.tensor([1., 2.])
>>> solver = tk.decompositions.LeastSquaresSolver()
>>> solution, record = solver.solve(matrix, target)
>>> torch.allclose(solution, target)
True
solve(environment, target, site=None, sweep=None, return_record=True, regularization_scale=None)[source]#

Solves one local system and optionally records its diagnostics.

A vector target produces a vector solution. Multiple right-hand sides share the same factorization. Diagnostics describe the original local system before column and system scaling; records are detached, while the solution retains its PyTorch autograd graph. No device fallback is performed.

Parameters

  • environment (torch.Tensor) – Real or complex design matrix with shape (n_rows, n_parameters).

  • target (torch.Tensor) – Right-hand side with shape (n_rows,) or (n_rows, n_targets), sharing the matrix device and dtype.

  • site (int or tuple[int], optional) – Site or block identifier attached to the local record.

  • sweep (int, optional) – Directional sweep identifier attached to the local record.

  • return_record (bool) – Whether to calculate residuals and create a LocalSolveRecord. Defaults to True. False skips diagnostic calculations.

  • regularization_scale (torch.Tensor, optional) – Non-negative scalar factor for the regularization coefficient when a caller has normalized both the design and target. Environment caches use it to preserve absolute Tikhonov regularization under that normalization.

Returns

Solution and optional diagnostics, including the effective least-squares driver. CPU driver retries remain on CPU; accelerator errors propagate.

Return type

tuple[torch.Tensor, LocalSolveRecord or None]

ALS objectives, samplers and environments#

These lower-level objects support custom objectives and execution. Ordinary fits configure sampling through SamplingPolicy rather than constructing environment caches or row samplers directly.

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.ALSProblem(source=None, observations=None, weights=None, mask=None, sampled=False)[source]#

Defines the values and weighted L2 objective of an ALS fit.

source describes a known finite tensor. observations instead uses the stored support of a SparseTensorSource as the permanent set of known entries. In that objective, entries outside the support are unknown and never queried. This interpretation belongs to the problem; an ordinary sparse source still represents zeros outside its support.

Residual weights multiply the differences before their squared norm is taken: \(\|W(\widehat{T}-T)\|_2^2\). A mask gives zero weight to excluded entries. Sampling is performed by the backend. Sampled fits measure complete-sweep errors on a separate, fixed evaluation set whose target values are cached by prepare_evaluation().

Parameters

  • source (BaseSource, optional) – Finite scalar tensor source. Required without observations.

  • observations (SparseTensorSource, optional) – Stored scalar observations. Their order is support order, including explicitly stored zero values. Sparse construction coalesces repeated indices by summing their values before this objective is formed.

  • weights (torch.Tensor, optional) – Non-negative multiplicative residual weights. Shape is in_dim for a known source or (n_observations,) in stored support order for an observed objective.

  • mask (BaseSource, optional) – Boolean scalar tensor source with the same dimensions and device as source. True entries participate. Use either a mask or an explicit observation objective.

  • sampled (bool) – Whether a backend selects renewable samples from a known source. Defaults to False. Observations always define a fixed objective. Sampled fits prepare independent evaluation entries before sweeping.

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.DenseTensorSource(torch.ones(2, 3))
>>> problem = tk.decompositions.ALSProblem(source)
>>> problem.in_dim, problem.has_fixed_objective
((2, 3), True)
property in_dim#

Dimensions of all represented tensor variables.

property out_shape#

Shape of each evaluated value, when already known.

property has_fixed_objective#

Whether a fixed complete-sweep error measurement is available.

prepare_evaluation(n_samples=16384, generator=None)[source]#

Caches fixed target entries for complete-sweep error measurements.

Uniform entries are drawn with replacement using a private CPU random stream. The supplied generator and global random states are unchanged. All entries are used when the budget covers the tensor, or for an observation objective. Residual weights and masks are cached too.

Parameters

  • n_samples (int, optional) – Number of uniform evaluation entries. Defaults to 16384. None requests exact evaluation of the complete objective.

  • generator (torch.Generator, optional) – Base seed for the independent evaluation stream. Its initial seed plus one is used; omission uses the global initial seed plus one.

property evaluation_info#

Describes the exact or fixed-sample error used by this fit.

evaluation_error(approximation)[source]#

Measures the weighted error on the prepared evaluation entries.

The absolute norm is scaled to estimate the complete objective norm. The relative norm uses the weighted target norm on the same entries; it is a ratio estimate when the evaluation is sampled.

Parameters

approximation (torch.Tensor) – Current approximation in _evaluation_indices order, with one scalar per entry. Original target values are not queried again.

Returns

Absolute and relative objective errors. Whether these are sampled estimates is recorded in evaluation_info.

Return type

tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]

evaluate(configurations)[source]#

Evaluates a known source at the supplied configurations.

Parameters

configurations (ConfigurationBatch) – Discrete indices in the source’s in_sites order.

Returns

One target value per configuration. Observation-only problems expose their targets through observations.support_values.

Return type

torch.Tensor

entry_weights(indices)[source]#

Returns residual weights for selected scalar tensor entries.

Parameters

indices (torch.Tensor) – Integer configurations with shape (n_entries, n_sites). Observed problems require indices on their stored support.

Returns

One weight per entry, or None for an unweighted objective.

Return type

torch.Tensor or None

objective_error(approximation, configurations=None)[source]#

Computes absolute and relative weighted L2 residual norms.

Parameters

  • approximation (torch.Tensor) – Approximate values in configuration order or stored observation order, with one scalar value per entry.

  • configurations (ConfigurationBatch, optional) – Configurations for a known source objective. Omit for observations.

Returns

Absolute residual norm and its ratio to the weighted target norm. A zero target gives zero relative error for an exact fit and infinity otherwise.

Return type

tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.TTLeverageRows(cores, uniform_mix=0.0)[source]#

Samples TT local-design rows from mixed-canonical leverage scores.

The exact mixed-canonical construction follows Efficient Leverage Score Sampling for Tensor Train Decomposition (2024), available in this paper by Vivek Bharadwaj, Beheshteh T. Rakhshan, Osman Asif Malik and Guillaume Rabusseau.

The current cores are obtained from cores at every draw. Cores to the left of the selected site must be left-isometric, and cores to its right right-isometric. Under this invariant, the leverage distribution factors into left row norms, a uniform current input and right row norms, so rows are sampled recursively without materializing the full local design.

uniform_mix mixes the normalized leverage distribution with a global uniform distribution. A positive value gives every row non-zero support. Importance weighting makes the sampled Gram matrix and right-hand side unbiased when support is sufficient; it does not make the nonlinear least-squares solution itself an unbiased estimator.

Parameters

  • cores (callable) – Returns the current standard cores whenever a distribution is built. Each core has shape (left rank, input, right rank). The callback exposes updates without copying or retaining an obsolete decomposition.

  • uniform_mix (float) – Uniform proposal weight in [0, 1]. Default is zero. A positive value gives every global row nonzero probability; draw probabilities always include the mixture and stay attached to the sampled rows.

probabilities(site, configurations)[source]#

Returns proposal probabilities for selected global configurations.

Parameters

  • site (int) – Active site whose local system defines the proposal.

  • configurations (ConfigurationBatch) – Discrete configurations with one input per tensor site.

Returns

Real probabilities with shape (batch,).

Return type

torch.Tensor

draw(owner, site, n_samples, generator=None)[source]#

Draws recursive leverage rows and records proposal versions.

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.TRProductLeverageRows(cores, uniform_mix=0.0)[source]#

Samples an approximate product-leverage proposal for TR designs.

This implements the product proposal from Algorithm 2 of A Sampling-Based Method for Tensor Ring Decomposition (2021), available in this paper by Osman Asif Malik and Stephen Becker. For every core outside the active site, it computes row leverage scores of the mode-input unfolding with shape (input, left rank * right rank). Their product bounds the leverage distribution of the complete cyclic design, but is not that exact distribution, so batches are labelled proposal_exact=False.

The published algorithm samples environment configurations and retains the full active input fiber. Accordingly, n_samples counts environments; the returned batch contains n_samples * in_dim[site] scalar rows. Expanding fibers is a TensorKrowch row-interface adaptation and preserves the paper’s sampling weights.

uniform_mix adds global uniform support. Importance weights always use the actual mixed draw probability, so sampled Gram matrices and right-hand sides target the full row objective even though the proposal is only an approximation to leverage scores.

Parameters

  • cores (callable) – Returns the current standard cores whenever a distribution is built. Each core has shape (left rank, input, right rank). The callback exposes updates without copying or retaining an obsolete decomposition.

  • uniform_mix (float) – Uniform proposal weight in [0, 1]. Default is zero. A positive value gives every global row nonzero probability; draw probabilities always include the mixture and stay attached to the sampled rows.

probabilities(site, configurations)[source]#

Returns proposal probabilities for selected global configurations.

Parameters

  • site (int) – Active site whose local system defines the proposal.

  • configurations (ConfigurationBatch) – Discrete configurations with one input per tensor site.

Returns

Real probabilities with shape (batch,).

Return type

torch.Tensor

draw(owner, site, n_samples, generator=None)[source]#

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.TRExactLeverageRows(cores, uniform_mix=0.0)[source]#

Samples exact leverage rows of a cyclic TR local design.

This specializes Sections 4.1–4.2 and Appendix B.2 of Sampling-Based Decomposition Algorithms for Arbitrary Tensor Networks (2022), available in this paper by Osman Asif Malik, Vivek Bharadwaj and Riley Murray, to a TR one-site ALS environment. It contracts the double-layer Gram matrix, computes its small pseudoinverse and draws the joint input configuration sequentially from exact conditional probabilities. The exponentially tall design matrix and its complete leverage vector are never formed.

As in the paper, n_samples counts environment configurations and every selected environment retains the complete active input fiber. TensorKrowch additionally permits uniform_mix for full-support robustness. A mixed proposal still stores and uses its exact draw probabilities, although only uniform_mix=0 is the pure leverage distribution analyzed in the paper.

Parameters

  • cores (callable) – Returns the current standard cores whenever a distribution is built. Each core has shape (left rank, input, right rank). The callback exposes updates without copying or retaining an obsolete decomposition.

  • uniform_mix (float) – Uniform proposal weight in [0, 1]. Default is zero. A positive value gives every global row nonzero probability; draw probabilities always include the mixture and stay attached to the sampled rows.

probabilities(site, configurations)[source]#

Returns proposal probabilities for selected global configurations.

Parameters

  • site (int) – Active site whose local system defines the proposal.

  • configurations (ConfigurationBatch) – Discrete configurations with one input per tensor site.

Returns

Real probabilities with shape (batch,).

Return type

torch.Tensor

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.TTEnvironmentCache(cores, core_versions=None, renormalize=False)[source]#

Zip-up TT environment cache for exact and sampled ALS sweeps.

A forward sweep precomputes old right suffixes and grows a prefix from committed cores. A reverse sweep mirrors the process. Cores touched by a local solve, gauge absorption or scalar normalization are committed in one atomic update; only cached contractions that depend on those cores are rebuilt.

Parameters

  • cores (sequence of torch.Tensor) – Standard TT cores with shape (left rank, input, right rank) and unit boundary ranks.

  • core_versions (sequence of int, optional) – Initial version of every core. Defaults to zero.

  • renormalize (bool, optional) – Whether intermediate prefixes/suffixes are divided by one global norm. The active design’s accumulated scale is retained as log_scale.

Examples

>>> cache = tk.decompositions.TTEnvironmentCache(
...     [torch.ones(1, 2, 1), torch.ones(1, 3, 1)])
>>> cache.prepare_sweep((0, 1))
>>> cache.design(0).shape
torch.Size([6, 2])

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.TRSegmentEnvironmentCache(cores, n_segments=None, core_versions=None, renormalize=False)[source]#

Segmented zip-up cache for exact and sampled TR ALS sweeps.

Sites are partitioned into contiguous segments. Within the active segment, old suffixes are combined with a growing updated prefix (and conversely in reverse sweeps). Segment summaries provide the remaining cyclic path. All products follow the ring orientation and no inverse or pseudoinverse is used.

Parameters

  • cores (sequence of torch.Tensor) – Standard TR cores with shape (left rank, input, right rank).

  • n_segments (int, optional) – Number of balanced contiguous segments. Defaults to at most three.

  • core_versions (sequence of int, optional) – Initial version of every core. Defaults to zero.

  • renormalize (bool, optional) – Whether intermediate matrix products remove one global norm and retain the accumulated scale logarithmically.

Examples

>>> cache = tk.decompositions.TRSegmentEnvironmentCache(
...     [torch.ones(2, 2, 2), torch.ones(2, 3, 2)])
>>> cache.prepare_sweep((0, 1))
>>> cache.design(0).shape
torch.Size([6, 8])

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.ALSSweepDriver[source]#

Runs directional sweeps without topology-specific contractions.

The backend owns environment construction and local solves. This driver chooses sweep directions, requests complete site updates, measures complete-sweep objectives, applies convergence and emits structured events.

fit(problem, backend, convergence=None, observer=None, collect_metrics=False, phase='ALS', *, sweep_direction='forward', generator=None)[source]#

Runs ALS until a normalized stopping reason is reached.

sweep_direction="forward" visits sites in increasing order on every sweep. "alternating" reverses that order on odd sweeps. Each directional pass counts once toward max_sweeps.

Parameters

  • problem (ALSProblem) – Target values, residual weights and fixed-objective semantics.

  • backend (ALSBackend) – Owns the cores, local solves and environment updates. Each local solution replaces the active core before moving its gauge.

  • convergence (ConvergencePolicy, optional) – Complete-sweep stopping criteria. Defaults to ten sweeps.

  • observer (DecompositionObserver, optional) – Receives structured progress events. Its lifecycle belongs to the calling decomposition, which closes it after finalizing results.

  • collect_metrics (bool) – Whether to retain local solve and sweep records. Defaults to False.

  • phase (str) – Label attached to progress events. Defaults to "ALS".

  • sweep_direction ({"forward", "alternating"}) – Internal traversal selected by the decomposition: alternating directions for TT and forward passes for TR.

  • generator (torch.Generator, optional) – Base seed for the independent evaluation stream in sampled fits. Its state is not advanced.

Returns

Final cores, optional metrics, completed sweep count and stopping reason. Stagnation alone does not certify a small residual.

Return type

ALSSweepDriver

Ring conversion and spectral functions#

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.TT2TR(tt, out_device='cpu')[source]#

Converts an open tensor train into a tensor ring.

Optimization openers use center-out gauge transport with optional residual expansion. BLOSTR openers instead recover an exact central opening and absorb its gauges outward, splitting with SVDs. Input cores remain unchanged. Spectral factors and the working TT cores use a common complex dtype, so BLOSTR conversion returns complex cores even for real inputs.

Parameters

  • tt (TT, MPS or sequence of torch.Tensor) – Open tensor train, open-boundary MPS or cores in standard TT order. Structural batches are not supported.

  • out_device (str or torch.device, optional) – Device for the returned cores. Default is "cpu"; None keeps the input device.

fit(rank=None, center=None, loop_opener='als', recursion='adjoint', *, block_boundaries=True, enrich=True, enrich_rank=None, enrich_rtol=1e-12, rtol=None, collect_metrics=False, verbose=0)[source]#

Fits right-link ranks and optionally truncates SVD splits adaptively.

A prescribed rank starts at center and grows an initial block when one site has insufficient physical capacity, then proceeds sitewise. By default, boundary sites are grouped into blocks, whose gauges are absorbed before SVD splitting. Overlapping blocks merge; the whole chain may be opened at once. With known ranks, boundary blocking can be disabled independently of the initial block. Discovery first fits one physical supercore for the central block and splits it with SVDs to determine its internal ranks. Prescribed blocks instead optimize their physical cores individually. Discovery is a numerical rank heuristic, not unique rank recovery.

Parameters

  • rank (int or sequence of int, optional) – Local ALS rank, or one right-link rank per core including the cyclic last entry. At SVD splits these are upper bounds: rtol may select smaller ranks, which are returned without zero padding. None discovers ranks using SVDs or spectral multiplicities.

  • center (int, optional) – Initial site, or the center of the discovery block. Defaults to the middle site.

  • loop_opener (str or LoopOpener, optional) – "als" optimizes local openings. "blostr" uses complete spectral recovery; "blostr_svd" recovers the first factor spectrally and splits the remainder with SVDs. Configured opener objects expose solver, convergence and projection options.

  • recursion (str or GaugeRecursion, optional) – "adjoint" moves QR centers or uses stored Vidal isometries; "pinv" uses TT-core pseudoinverses; "orth" dualizes the learned gauge. Configured objects accept PyTorch pseudoinverse keyword options. Exact BLOSTR conversion does not use transport.

  • block_boundaries (bool) – Group boundary sites into automatic blocks before gauge absorption and SVD splitting. Default is True. False keeps one-site boundaries and requires supplied rank for optimization openers. The initial block still grows automatically. Exact spectral conversion does not use this option.

  • enrich (bool) – Append orthogonal residual constraints without changing TR ranks. Default is True. Exact BLOSTR conversion does not use expansion.

  • enrich_rank (int, optional) – Maximum orthogonal coordinates added per transition. None retains all significant directions; zero adds none.

  • enrich_rtol (float) – Residual singular-value cutoff relative to the opened factor’s Frobenius norm. Default is 1e-12.

  • rtol (float, optional) – Relative discarded squared singular-value mass for rank discovery and block SVD splits. Default None truncates only to rank when ranks are supplied. A tolerance can reduce SVD ranks below these bounds. With no ranks, omitted rtol uses 1e-12 for discovery, bounded below by machine precision. Spectral conversion also uses the tolerance for reconstruction checks. It does not define ALS convergence.

  • collect_metrics (bool) – Retain local solver and decomposition diagnostics. Final fidelity and reconstruction error are always measured.

  • verbose (bool or int) – Console verbosity from 0 (silent) to 3 (final cores included).

Returns

Cores in site order, metrics and construction metadata.

Return type

TRDecomposition

Examples

>>> tt = tk.formats.TT([torch.ones(2, 1), torch.ones(1, 2)])
>>> result = tk.decompositions.TT2TR(tt).fit(rank=1)
>>> result.rank
[1, 1]
tensorkrowch.decompositions.tt2tr(tt, rank=None, center=None, loop_opener='als', recursion='adjoint', *, block_boundaries=True, enrich=True, enrich_rank=None, enrich_rtol=1e-12, rtol=None, out_device='cpu', collect_metrics=False, verbose=0)[source]#

Converts a tensor train to a tensor ring.

Use TT2TR for repeated fits of one input tensor train. All arguments have the same meaning as in TT2TR.fit().

Parameters

  • tt (TT, MPS or sequence of torch.Tensor) – Open tensor train, open-boundary MPS or cores in standard TT order.

  • rank (int or sequence of int, optional) – Local ALS rank or one right-link rank per core, including the closing link. At SVD splits these are upper bounds; rtol may reduce them. None discovers the rank profile. No zero padding is applied.

  • center (int, optional) – Initial site or discovery-block center. Defaults to the middle site.

  • loop_opener (str or LoopOpener, optional) – Local strategy: "als", "blostr", "blostr_svd" or a configured opener object.

  • recursion (str or GaugeRecursion, optional) – "adjoint", "pinv", "orth" or a configured strategy. Exact spectral conversion does not use gauge recursion.

  • block_boundaries (bool) – Group boundary sites into automatic blocks before gauge absorption and SVD splitting. Default is True. False keeps one-site boundaries and requires supplied rank for optimization openers. The initial block still grows automatically. Exact spectral conversion does not use this option.

  • enrich (bool) – Whether to append orthogonal residual constraints. Default is True.

  • enrich_rank (int, optional) – Maximum auxiliary coordinates per transition. None retains all significant directions.

  • enrich_rtol (float) – Relative residual singular-value threshold. Default is 1e-12.

  • rtol (float, optional) – Relative SVD tail-energy tolerance for discovery and block splits. Default None truncates only to rank when ranks are supplied; discovery without ranks uses 1e-12.

  • out_device (str or torch.device, optional) – Final core device. Default is "cpu"; None keeps the input device.

  • collect_metrics (bool) – Whether to retain local diagnostics. Final error is always measured.

  • verbose (bool or int) – Console verbosity from 0 (silent) to 3 (final cores included).

Returns

Tensor ring cores, reconstruction metrics and construction metadata.

Return type

TRDecomposition

tensorkrowch.decompositions.tr_blostr(tensor, rank=None, *, slices=None, projection='slices', spectral_atol=1e-10, n_attempts=8, n_iters=50, n_restarts=10, generator=None, out_device='cpu', collect_metrics=False, verbose=0)[source]#

Recovers a dense tensor ring using spectral BLOSTR at every site.

Two pairs of interior slices identify the first core through blockwise simultaneous diagonalization. Product Gaussian projections of all but two physical axes then recover each remaining core by a linear solve. These avoid singular coordinate slices of otherwise injective cores. This is the uniform-rank construction of Algorithm 1 in A Provably Efficient Method for Tensor Ring Decomposition and Its Applications. It targets exact tensors with injective physical unfoldings at every site and nondegenerate projection ratios. Each physical dimension must therefore be at least the squared TR rank. This differs from tr_blostr_svd(), which needs injectivity only at its two external physical axes. No accuracy guarantee is made for approximate inputs or rank-deficient recovery environments.

Parameters

  • tensor (torch.Tensor) – Dense tensor with one physical axis per future TR core.

  • rank (int or sequence[int], optional) – Prescribed right-link ranks, including the cyclic last entry. Full BLOSTR requires equal ranks. With None, balanced k-means discovers the multiplicities of the nonzero spectrum and requires them to imply equal cyclic and adjacent ranks.

  • slices (sequence of four index sequences, optional) – Configurations fixing every interior axis for the two spectral ratios. With None, configurations are drawn using generator.

  • projection ({"slices", "gaussian"}) – Coordinate slices or contractions against four independent dense Gaussian tensors over all interior axes. The latter can span matrix directions absent from any single coordinate slice. Explicit slices require "slices".

  • spectral_atol (float) – Absolute eigenvalue cutoff and relative within-cluster tolerance used when discovering balanced spectral multiplicities. A machine-precision floor is applied to both tests. Default is 1e-10.

  • n_attempts (int) – Number of independent spectral attempts. Default is 8; explicit slices use one attempt. The smallest reconstruction error is kept.

  • n_iters (int) – Balanced k-means iteration and restart budgets. Defaults are 50 and 10.

  • n_restarts (int) – Balanced k-means iteration and restart budgets. Defaults are 50 and 10.

  • generator (torch.Generator, optional) – Controls spectral projections, balanced clustering and recovery projections.

  • out_device (str or torch.device, optional) – Final core storage device. None keeps the input device.

  • collect_metrics (bool) – Whether to retain reconstruction, truncation and timing diagnostics.

  • verbose (bool or int) – Console verbosity from 0 (silent) to 3.

Returns

Recovered TR cores and construction metadata. Spectral factors use a complex dtype even for real input tensors.

Return type

TRDecomposition

Examples

>>> cores = [torch.randn(1, 3, 1, dtype=torch.float64) for _ in range(3)]
>>> tensor = tk.formats.TR(cores).contract_dense()
>>> result = tk.decompositions.tr_blostr(tensor, rank=1)
>>> torch.allclose(result.contract_dense(), tensor.to(torch.complex128))
True
tensorkrowch.decompositions.tr_blostr_svd(tensor, rank=None, *, slices=None, projection='slices', spectral_atol=1e-10, n_attempts=8, n_iters=50, n_restarts=10, generator=None, cutoff=None, atol=None, rtol=None, cum_percentage=None, out_device='cpu', collect_metrics=False, verbose=0)[source]#

Recovers the first TR core spectrally and splits the rest with TT-SVD.

Unlike tr_blostr(), interior ranks may differ. The two ranks bounding the projected interior chain must coincide: rank[0] == rank[-2]. The cyclic rank may differ. Gaussian joint projections can retain full matrix rank even when an intermediate bond makes each coordinate slice deficient. The physical first and last axes must both have dimension at least rank[-1] * rank[0]. These conditions permit spectral recovery; they do not guarantee spectral separation for a particular projection.

Parameters

  • tensor (torch.Tensor) – Dense tensor with one physical axis per future TR core.

  • rank (int or sequence[int], optional) – Prescribed right-link ranks, including the cyclic last entry. With None, balanced k-means discovers the first cyclic and adjacent ranks; TT-SVD discovers the remaining bonds numerically.

  • slices (sequence of four index sequences, optional) – Configurations fixing every interior axis for the two spectral ratios. With None, configurations are drawn using generator.

  • projection ({"slices", "gaussian"}) – Coordinate slices or contractions against four independent dense Gaussian tensors over all interior axes. The latter can span matrix directions absent from any single coordinate slice. Explicit slices require "slices".

  • spectral_atol (float) – Absolute eigenvalue cutoff and relative within-cluster tolerance used when discovering balanced spectral multiplicities. A machine-precision floor is applied to both tests. Default is 1e-10.

  • n_attempts (int) – Number of independent spectral attempts. Default is 8; explicit slices use one attempt. The smallest reconstruction error is kept.

  • n_iters (int) – Balanced k-means iteration and restart budgets. Defaults are 50 and 10.

  • n_restarts (int) – Balanced k-means iteration and restart budgets. Defaults are 50 and 10.

  • generator (torch.Generator, optional) – Controls spectral projections, balanced clustering and recovery projections.

  • cutoff (float, optional) – Singular values at or below this value are discarded in tail TT-SVD.

  • atol (float, optional) – Absolute or relative discarded-energy tolerance, or retained squared singular-value fraction, in tail TT-SVD. With no rank or tolerance, a numerical threshold accounts for the precision and conditioning of the recovered first core. A supplied rank is an upper bound; smaller retained ranks are returned without zero padding.

  • rtol (float, optional) – Absolute or relative discarded-energy tolerance, or retained squared singular-value fraction, in tail TT-SVD. With no rank or tolerance, a numerical threshold accounts for the precision and conditioning of the recovered first core. A supplied rank is an upper bound; smaller retained ranks are returned without zero padding.

  • cum_percentage (float, optional) – Absolute or relative discarded-energy tolerance, or retained squared singular-value fraction, in tail TT-SVD. With no rank or tolerance, a numerical threshold accounts for the precision and conditioning of the recovered first core. A supplied rank is an upper bound; smaller retained ranks are returned without zero padding.

  • out_device (str or torch.device, optional) – Final core storage device. None keeps the input device.

  • collect_metrics (bool) – Whether to retain reconstruction, truncation and timing diagnostics.

  • verbose (bool or int) – Console verbosity from 0 (silent) to 3.

Returns

Recovered TR cores and construction metadata. Spectral factors use a complex dtype even for real input tensors.

Return type

TRDecomposition

Examples

>>> cores = [torch.randn(1, 3, 1, dtype=torch.float64) for _ in range(3)]
>>> tensor = tk.formats.TR(cores).contract_dense()
>>> result = tk.decompositions.tr_blostr_svd(tensor, rank=1)
>>> torch.allclose(result.contract_dense(), tensor.to(torch.complex128))
True

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.LoopOpener(*args, **kwargs)[source]#

Solves one local cyclic factorization with explicit gauge constraints.

An opening represents its target as left gauge, input core(s) and right gauge. Capabilities declare whether a strategy accepts either or both fixed gauges and whether it supports multiple input cores. Fixed gauges must be preserved exactly. The target and gauge recursion are independent of the opener.

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.QRLoopOpener(opener='als', refinement_sweeps=1)[source]#

Balances free external axes with QR before opening a local tensor ring.

The right axis is factorized first, followed by the left axis using QR of its adjoint. Both factorizations retain their complete reduced bases: there is no singular-value threshold or TR-rank cap. Triangular factors are kept outside the initial objective and restored in the returned gauges. Inherited fixed gauges and their external axes are unchanged.

Parameters

  • opener (str or LoopOpener, optional) – Local strategy applied to the balanced target. Default is "als".

  • refinement_sweeps (int, optional) – Additional ALS sweeps on the original target after restoring the factors. Default is one. Zero disables refinement. A candidate that increases the local residual is rejected. This does not guarantee a smaller global reconstruction error.

Examples

>>> opener = tk.decompositions.QRLoopOpener(refinement_sweeps=1)
>>> opener.capabilities.supports_blocks
True
property capabilities#

Returns the wrapped solver’s gauge and block constraints.

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.AdjointGaugeRecursion(**pinv_kwargs)[source]#

Transports opened factors through directional TT isometries.

For an ordinary TT, TT2TR first prepares a mixed canonical form. Each transition factorizes the source core or contracted block as \(B=QF\), transports with \(Q^H\), and absorbs \(F\) into the next reference target. This preserves the input tensor while moving its orthogonality center independently along the two outward branches.

A valid VidalGauge instead supplies the isometries directly. Stored Schmidt powers are removed or absorbed on both sides before applying the adjoint; powers may differ at each bond. The input’s local targets and their ALS metric are retained. Explicit, implicit and inverse Vidal therefore share the same transport strategy.

Parameters

**pinv_kwargs – Accepted for the common recursion interface. The directional adjoint and its numerical-rank diagnostics do not use these options. Optional TT2TR expansion adds orthogonal residual coordinates and zero reference rows without changing TR ranks.

Examples

>>> recursion = tk.decompositions.AdjointGaugeRecursion()
class tensorkrowch.decompositions.PinvGaugeRecursion(**pinv_kwargs)[source]#

Transports learned TR factors through the local TT-core pseudoinverse.

For the directional TT unfolding \(M\) and the factor \(X\) formed by the incoming gauge and recovered TR core, the next gauge is \(E=M^+X\). An initial multi-site block is contracted and inverted as a whole. Components outside the column space of \(M\) are allowed.

Parameters

**pinv_kwargs – atol, rtol and hermitian forwarded to torch.linalg.pinv(). Tolerances must be numbers or real scalar tensors; batched gauge maps are not supported.

Examples

>>> recursion = tk.decompositions.PinvGaugeRecursion(rtol=1e-12)
class tensorkrowch.decompositions.OrthGaugeRecursion(**pinv_kwargs)[source]#

Transports using the pseudoinverse of the learned outgoing gauge.

The outgoing right gauge is dualized and mirrored into the next fixed left gauge. The leftward operation is its mirror. The induced support projector is orthogonal; deficient rank is allowed.

Parameters

**pinv_kwargs – atol, rtol and hermitian forwarded to torch.linalg.pinv(). Tolerances must be numbers or real scalar tensors; batched gauge maps are not supported.

Examples

>>> recursion = tk.decompositions.OrthGaugeRecursion(rtol=1e-12)
>>> isinstance(recursion, tk.decompositions.GaugeRecursion)
True

Builds the fixed right gauge for the next site to the left.

Builds the fixed left gauge for the next site to the right.

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.GaugeMap(core, orientation, site=None, _reference_matrix=None, _pinv_kwargs=<factory>, records=(), metadata=<factory>)[source]#

Represents a map between a TT bond and two TR bonds.

A left gauge has shape (cyclic_rank, external_dim, local_rank) and a right gauge has shape (local_rank, external_dim, cyclic_rank). Both orientations expose the same matrix layout through matrix. pinv() returns its directional dual. The transpose in that dual is not conjugated because tensor network bonds contract bilinearly.

Parameters

  • core (torch.Tensor) – Three-dimensional floating or complex gauge tensor.

  • orientation ({"left", "right"}) – Which external gauge is represented by core.

  • site (int, optional) – Destination site used in diagnostics.

  • records (sequence of GaugeRecord) – Optional measurements from the transport that produced this map.

  • metadata (mapping) – Optional transport diagnostics, copied when the map is constructed.

Examples

>>> gauge = tk.decompositions.GaugeMap(
...     torch.eye(2).reshape(1, 2, 2), 'left')
>>> gauge.pinv().matrix.shape
torch.Size([2, 2])
property matrix#

Returns shape (external_dim, cyclic_rank * local_rank).

property cyclic_rank#

Cyclic rank encoded by this orientation.

property local_rank#

Adjacent TR rank encoded by this orientation.

property is_dual#

Whether this map was constructed as a directional dual.

Swaps the two TR axes while preserving the matrix representation.

pinv(**pinv_kwargs)[source]#

Constructs the directional dual with a Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse.

Parameters

**pinv_kwargs – atol, rtol and hermitian forwarded to torch.linalg.pinv(). Tolerances must be numbers or real scalar tensors; batched gauge maps are not supported.

Returns

Dual with the same external and TR dimensions. Rank-deficient maps retain their support projector; no cancellation is enforced.

Return type

GaugeMap

Sketching engines and functions#

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.TTRSS(source, embedding=None, in_dim=None, domain=None, domain_multiplier=1, out_position=None, *, device=None, dtype=None, out_device='cpu', input_fitter=None, range_projector=None, transform=None, local_solver=None)[source]#

Reusable Tensor Train Recursive Sketching from Samples problem.

The fixed object stores the function (or BaseSource), embedding, domain and output layout. Each fit() receives a sample set and its truncation options, and returns a lightweight TTDecomposition. The result cores can initialize an MPS directly with tk.models.MPS(tensors=result.cores).

A shared embedding and domain are broadcast to every input site; sequences select site-dependent values. Tensor-valued outputs are split into one basis-embedded site per output axis, placed as evenly as possible by default. Metadata that depends on sketch_samples is normalized independently in every fit, so repeating a fit does not retain mutable numerical state.

Directional SVDs select the retained subspaces and absorb their singular values into the local tensors. Only the center keeps the isometric lifting maps needed to start both sketch recursions.

source defines how inputs are evaluated. Accepted finite sources are DenseTensorSource, SparseTensorSource, FormatSource, CallableTensorSource and CallableQuanticsSource; tensors are wrapped automatically. Wrap a non-Quantics format or MPS in FormatSource. Continuous functions use CallableSource or a raw callable and require an embedding. Finite sources use basis embeddings by default. The dense, sparse and callable source classes provide .matrix(...) constructors for paired input/output dimensions; FormatSource obtains these from a matrix format. Structural batches are not supported.

Parameters

  • source (BaseSource, torch.Tensor or callable) – Input values and their evaluation rules; continuous inputs also require an embedding.

  • embedding (callable, torch.Tensor or sequence, optional) – Shared embedding or one per input site. Required for continuous sources. An embedding maps site values to vectors of size in_dim.

  • in_dim (int or sequence[int], optional) – Expected embedding dimensions; otherwise inferred from embeddings.

  • domain (torch.Tensor or sequence of torch.Tensor, optional) – Domain values used to fit the embeddings, inferred from samples when omitted. Finite sources supply their index domains by default.

  • domain_multiplier (int) – Maximum inferred-domain size in multiples of the embedding dimension.

  • out_position (int or sequence[int], optional) – Positions of response sites in a vector chain. Matrix sources place each output site next to its input before combining their cores.

  • device (str or torch.device, optional) – Evaluation device. Existing sources retain their device.

  • dtype (torch.dtype, optional) – Declared function output dtype. Existing sources retain their dtype.

  • out_device (str or torch.device, optional) – Device receiving completed cores; None retains the source device.

  • input_fitter (InputFitter or sequence of InputFitter, optional) – Shared fitter or one per input/output axis in the expanded chain; inferred when omitted. Matrix pairs are combined after fitting.

  • range_projector (RangeProjector, optional) – Complete range-projection strategy. None uses direct SVD.

  • transform (callable, optional) – Called once with a ConfigurationMap. Returns transformed values with the same shape as its initial values table. Extra raw source evaluations are available through its evaluate method.

  • local_solver (LeastSquaresSolver, optional) – Solver for local core-determining equations.

Examples

>>> def function(data):
...     return data.prod(dim=1, keepdim=True)
>>> def embedding(data):
...     return torch.stack([data, 1 - data], dim=-1)
>>> samples = torch.rand(32, 3)
>>> decomposer = tk.decompositions.TTRSS(function, embedding)
>>> result = decomposer.fit(samples, rank=2)
>>> len(result.cores)
3
>>> model = tk.models.MPS(tensors=result.cores, parameterized=False)
>>> model.boundary
'obc'
fit(sketch_samples, labels=None, rank=None, *, center=None, cutoff=None, atol=None, rtol=None, cum_percentage=None, batch_size=64, generator=None, verbose=0, collect_metrics=False)[source]#

Fits a TT from correlated samples, starting at center.

All local queries are deduplicated and evaluated together. Each Phi then fits its physical axis and selects an outward singular subspace: both directions at the center, left on its left, right on its right. Spectra stay outside these bases. The cores are connected by local least-squares equations without a final rounding operation.

Parameters

  • sketch_samples (torch.Tensor, sequence or ConfigurationBatch) – Packed inputs with shape (batch_size, n_inputs, ...), or one tensor with leading batch dimension per source input.

  • labels (torch.Tensor, optional) – Flattened output-component indices with shape (batch_size,). When omitted, tensor outputs select indices with probabilities proportional to squared magnitudes. Scalar outputs need no labels.

  • rank (int or sequence[int], optional) – Shared maximum rank or one per open TT bond. None discovers numerical ranks under the truncation criteria. Matrix sources specify one rank between consecutive input/output pairs; each internal input/output split retains its full local capacity.

  • center (int, optional) – Initial site in the final chain, including output sites. Defaults to the middle. An endpoint gives a single outward branch. Matrix inputs and outputs occupy separate sites before pairing cores.

  • cutoff (float, optional) – Minimum singular value to keep. Values <= cutoff are removed.

  • atol (float, optional) – Maximum discarded sum of squared singular values.

  • rtol (float, optional) – Maximum discarded sum of squared singular values divided by their total sum of squares. Must lie in [0, 1].

  • cum_percentage (float, optional) – Minimum retained squared singular-value fraction. Equivalent to rtol=1-cum_percentage.

  • batch_size (int) – Maximum number of unique configurations evaluated together.

  • generator (torch.Generator, optional) – Generator for domain subsampling, labels and randomized projectors.

  • verbose (bool or int) – Level from 0 to 3: silent, progress, local details, core tensors.

  • collect_metrics (bool) – Retains evaluation, fitting, truncation, solve and timing records.

Returns

TT result, or the corresponding matrix/Quantics result when the source declares that structure. Cores are stored on out_device.

Return type

TTDecomposition

Examples

>>> tensor = torch.arange(16.).reshape(2, 2, 2, 2)
>>> samples = torch.cartesian_prod(*[torch.arange(2)] * 4)
>>> result = tk.decompositions.TTRSS(tensor).fit(
...     samples, rank=2, center=2)
>>> result.in_dim
(2, 2, 2, 2)
class tensorkrowch.decompositions.TRRSS(source, embedding=None, in_dim=None, domain=None, domain_multiplier=1, out_position=None, *, device=None, dtype=None, out_device='cpu', input_fitter=None, range_projector=None, transform=None, local_solver=None)[source]#

Fits a tensor ring from correlated source samples.

Construction arguments are those of TTRSS. The two algorithms share evaluation, global transformation, physical fitting and directional SVDs. TR-RSS then aligns an intermediate TT, contracts its central/end blocks and opens the central loop. Singular spectra remain absorbed in the local tensors. A QRLoopOpener can balance these targets and refine after restoring its factors. Subsequent sites retain the full inherited sketch space, so sketch recursion can preserve constraints outside the rank selected by an outgoing SVD.

No new source-query Phi is constructed for a block. The intermediate TT alignment can introduce approximation error; it is measured separately from local loop-opening residuals when metrics are requested. The tt_alignment error is measured on the supplied sketch samples, or on the shared configuration table when transform changes target values. It is a residual of the intermediate TT, rather than an error bound for the final ring.

Examples

>>> samples = torch.cartesian_prod(*[torch.arange(2)] * 5)
>>> result = tk.decompositions.TRRSS(torch.ones(2, 2, 2, 2, 2)).fit(
...     samples, rank=1)
>>> result.rank
[1, 1, 1, 1, 1]
fit(sketch_samples, labels=None, rank=None, *, center=None, loop_opener='als', block_boundaries=True, cutoff=None, atol=None, rtol=None, cum_percentage=None, batch_size=64, generator=None, verbose=0, collect_metrics=False)[source]#

Opens an automatic central block and recurses toward both ends.

Parameters

  • sketch_samples (torch.Tensor, sequence or ConfigurationBatch) – Packed inputs with shape (batch_size, n_inputs, ...), or one tensor with leading batch dimension per source input.

  • labels (torch.Tensor, optional) – Flattened output-component indices with shape (batch_size,). When omitted, tensor outputs select indices with probabilities proportional to squared magnitudes. Scalar outputs need no labels.

  • rank (int or sequence[int], optional) – Shared maximum rank or one right-bond rank per final TR site; the last entry is cyclic. Phi TT-cut caps are cyclic rank times each internal rank. None discovers ranks from truncated TT blocks.

  • center (int, optional) – Seed site of the initial block. Defaults to the middle; blocks grow to provide sufficient physical capacity and merge at ends.

  • loop_opener (str or LoopOpener) – Local cyclic factorization, default "als". Configure ALS solvers and convergence through an ALSLoopOpener object. Use QRLoopOpener for local balancing and refinement.

  • block_boundaries (bool) – Selects injective end blocks. False keeps single-site ends and requires prescribed ranks.

  • cutoff (float, optional) – Minimum singular value to keep. Values <= cutoff are removed.

  • atol (float, optional) – Maximum discarded sum of squared singular values.

  • rtol (float, optional) – Maximum discarded sum of squared singular values divided by their total sum of squares. Must lie in [0, 1]. Also controls SVD splitting within end blocks, together with prescribed rank caps.

  • cum_percentage (float, optional) – Minimum retained squared singular-value fraction. Equivalent to rtol=1-cum_percentage.

  • batch_size (int) – Maximum number of unique configurations evaluated together.

  • generator (torch.Generator, optional) – Generator for domain subsampling, labels and local initializations.

  • verbose (bool or int) – Level from 0 to 3: silent, progress, local details, core tensors.

  • collect_metrics (bool) – Retains evaluation, fitting, truncation, solve and timing records.

Returns

Cyclic result, or its matrix/Quantics counterpart, on out_device.

Return type

TRDecomposition

Examples

>>> tensor = torch.ones(2, 3, 2, 3)
>>> samples = torch.cartesian_prod(
...     *[torch.arange(d) for d in tensor.shape])
>>> result = tk.decompositions.TRRSS(tensor).fit(samples, rank=1)
>>> result.in_dim
(2, 3, 2, 3)
class tensorkrowch.decompositions.TTRS(source, *, sketch_operator=None, transform=None, range_projector=None, out_device='cpu')[source]#

Projects a finite source and solves centered TT core equations.

Unlike TTRSS, TT-RS contracts a discrete source with recursive sketch operators, rather than taking pointwise sketch samples in fit. Sparse sources are contracted on their declared nonzero support; FormatSource uses structured contractions when available. Matrix and Quantics sources retain their result family. Structural batches are not supported.

The core-determining equations follow Generative modeling via tensor train sketching. Starting from an interior center and transforming individual Phi tensors are extensions; a generic transform need not preserve a common underlying tensor.

Parameters

  • source (BaseSource, TensorFormat1D, MPS or torch.Tensor) – Finite tensor input, with dimensions and evaluation defined by the source. Continuous callables require discretization first.

  • sketch_operator (SketchOperator, optional) – Recursive projections. Defaults to MarginalSketch().

  • transform (callable, optional) – Applied independently to each three-axis Phi before truncation. Must return a finite floating-point or complex tensor with the same shape and device; dtype promotion is allowed. Mathematical compatibility between transformed Phi tensors is the user’s choice.

  • range_projector (RangeProjector, optional) – Complete range-projection strategy. None uses direct SVD.

  • out_device (str or torch.device, optional) – Device receiving completed cores; None retains the source device.

Examples

>>> indices = torch.tensor([[0, 0, 0], [1, 1, 1]])
>>> source = tk.decompositions.SparseTensorSource.from_data(
...     indices, in_dim=(2, 2, 2))
>>> result = tk.decompositions.TTRS(
...     source, sketch_operator=tk.decompositions.SampledSketch()).fit(2)
>>> result.in_dim
(2, 2, 2)
fit(rank=None, *, center=None, cutoff=None, atol=None, rtol=None, cum_percentage=None, batch_size=None, generator=None, strict_system=False, verbose=0, collect_metrics=False)[source]#

Builds local Phi tensors and solves the two outward branches.

Parameters

  • center (int, optional) – Initial site. Defaults to the middle. An endpoint gives a single outward branch.

  • atol (float, optional) – Maximum discarded sum of squared singular values.

  • rtol (float, optional) – Maximum discarded sum of squared singular values divided by their total sum of squares. Must lie in [0, 1].

  • cum_percentage (float, optional) – Minimum retained squared singular-value fraction. Equivalent to rtol=1-cum_percentage.

  • batch_size (int, optional) – Maximum support or finite-grid evaluation batch size.

  • generator (torch.Generator, optional) – Generator for randomized sketches and projectors.

  • strict_system (bool) – Rejects coefficient matrices without the rank needed to identify all retained core coefficients.

  • verbose (bool or int) – Level from 0 to 3: silent, progress, local details, core tensors.

  • collect_metrics (bool) – Retains evaluation, truncation, solve and timing records.

Returns

TT result, or its matrix/Quantics counterpart, on out_device.

Return type

TTDecomposition

Examples

>>> tensor = torch.ones(2, 3, 2, 3)
>>> result = tk.decompositions.TTRS(tensor).fit(1, center=2)
>>> result.rank
[1, 1, 1]

Fits a sampled source with TT-RSS and returns a decomposition result.

Parameters follow TTRSS and TTRSS.fit(). sketch_samples contains the source inputs; finite sources supply basis embeddings by default, while continuous sources require embedding. rank bounds TT bonds, or bonds between matrix pairs, and center selects the initial site in the input/output-expanded chain. transform(configuration_map) acts once on the shared value table. Use the class for custom fitters, range projectors or local solvers.

Fits a Quantics source, using coordinate or encoded digit sketch samples.

source owns the layout and coordinate map. sample_space is "coordinates" (quantized to digit rows) or "digits" (already encoded rows). Remaining arguments follow TTRSS.fit(); transform follows TTRSS. Returns a Quantics decomposition, preserving matrix structure when supplied by the source.

>>> source = tk.decompositions.CallableQuanticsSource(
...     lambda x: 1 + x[:, 0], 1, base=2, level=2,
...     domain=torch.tensor([0., 1.]))

>>> result = tk.decompositions.qtt_rss(source, samples, rank=2)
>>> len(result.cores)
2

sample_space is "coordinates" (quantized to digit rows) or "digits" (already encoded rows). The source owns its layout and coordinate map. Remaining arguments follow TRRSS.fit(); transform follows TTRSS. Returns the Quantics decomposition, preserving matrix structure when supplied by the source.

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.TrainableEmbeddingFitter(model, in_dim=None, optimizer_factory=None, optimizer_kwargs=None, solver=None, max_steps=500, tolerance=1e-06, patience=50, fiber_batch_size=64, seed=0)[source]#

Fits a Phi axis with a locally trained embedding model.

model(domain) must return a matrix with shape (domain_size, in_dim). Training jointly optimizes the model and one temporary coefficient table against functional Phi fibers. A final shared least-squares solve removes optimizer error from the returned coefficients. Gradients and random state are confined to this fitter; the surrounding decomposition remains an ordinary numerical routine.

The trained model and a detached CPU state dictionary are attached to PhiOperator only when return_info=True. Otherwise the result contains only the fitted tensor and the model remains accessible as fitter.model.

Parameters

  • model (torch.nn.Module) – Embedding model returning shape (domain_size, in_dim).

  • in_dim (int, optional) – Expected model output dimension. Inferred from the model if omitted.

  • optimizer_factory (callable, optional) – Optimizer constructor. Defaults to torch.optim.Adam.

  • optimizer_kwargs (mapping, optional) – Optimizer arguments. Defaults to {'lr': 1e-2}.

  • solver (LeastSquaresSolver, optional) – Solver for the final coefficient fit. Defaults to LeastSquaresSolver.

  • max_steps (int) – Maximum optimizer steps. Default is 500.

  • tolerance (float) – Relative residual at which training stops. Default is 1e-6.

  • patience (int) – Consecutive steps without loss improvement before stopping. Default is 50.

  • fiber_batch_size (int, optional) – Number of functional Phi fibers collected together. None materializes the complete Phi; an existing tensor is used directly. Default is 64.

  • seed (int) – Seed for the local coefficient initialization. The caller’s random state is restored after training. Default is 0.

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.RandomizedRangeProjector(projection_dim=None, projection_oversampling=0, n_power_iter=0)[source]#

Approximates a matrix range using Gaussian projection and reduced QR.

For a flattened matrix \(M\), the method forms an orthonormal basis \(Q\) from a Gaussian projection and returns \(Q^H M\). Singular vectors of the smaller matrix are lifted by multiplication with \(Q\). Increasing the projection dimension or applying power iterations can improve the approximation at additional cost.

Parameters

  • projection_dim (int, optional) – Number of Gaussian vectors before oversampling. Defaults to the rank cap supplied to project(), or all columns if no cap is supplied.

  • projection_oversampling (int) – Extra Gaussian vectors beyond projection_dim. Default is 0. The total is capped at the number of matrix columns.

  • n_power_iter (int) – Stabilized power iterations, each alternating multiplication by the matrix adjoint and the matrix with reduced QR. Default is 0.

Examples

>>> projector = tk.decompositions.RandomizedRangeProjector(
...     projection_dim=2, projection_oversampling=1)
>>> projection = projector.project(torch.eye(3))
>>> torch.allclose(projection.reconstruct(), torch.eye(3), atol=1e-5)
True
