class tensorkrowch.decompositions.SampledSketch(samples=None, sketch_size=None)[source]#

Recursive one-hot sketches induced by correlated configurations.

For a sparse source the default configurations are its non-zero support. Prefix and suffix indicators select states from the same reference data. Missing sparse entries contribute their known zero without evaluation.

Parameters

  • samples (torch.Tensor or None, optional) – Reference index configurations with shape (batch, n_sites). None uses the source support or all states for a format source.

  • sketch_size (int or None, optional) – Maximum number of distinct prefix and suffix states at each cut. None retains every reference state.

>>> source = tk.decompositions.DenseTensorSource(torch.ones(2, 3, 2))
>>> system = tk.decompositions.SampledSketch().build(source)
>>> result = system.solve(rank=1)
>>> torch.allclose(result.contract_dense(), torch.ones(2, 3, 2))
True
class tensorkrowch.decompositions.MarginalSketch(order=1, factor=None)[source]#

Marginal sketches that retain a local neighborhood at every cut.

With order=1, this implements the neighbor-preserving sketches of Section 5.1 of Generative modeling via tensor train sketching (Hur, Hoskins, Lindsey, Stoudenmire and Khoo, 2022). Higher order values and an explicit contraction factor are TensorKrowch extensions of the same recursive marginal structure.

Parameters

  • order (int, optional) – Number of neighboring variables retained on each side of a cut.

  • factor (sequence of torch.Tensor or None, optional) – One vector of shape (in_dim[k],) per site. Their product weights source values before marginalization. None uses unweighted sums.

Examples

>>> source = tk.decompositions.DenseTensorSource(torch.ones(2, 3, 2))
>>> system = tk.decompositions.MarginalSketch().build(source)
>>> result = system.solve(rank=1, center=1)
>>> torch.allclose(result.contract_dense(), torch.ones(2, 3, 2))
True
class tensorkrowch.decompositions.TTStackSketch(tt_rank=1, stack_size=1, orthogonal=False)[source]#

Stack of Gaussian TT sketches with configurable size and internal rank.

stack_size is the number of TT sketches in each left or right stack.

tt_rank=1 is the separable Khatri-Rao limit. stack_size=1 is one Gaussian TT projection with tt_rank output rows at every partial cut. The full partial-sketch dimension is stack_size * tt_rank. Setting orthogonal=True selects a separately labelled orthogonalized variant; it does not claim the iid-Gaussian guarantees of the default construction.

The random cores follow Definition 3.1 of Linear-scaling Tensor Train Sketching by Paul Cazeaux, Mi-Song Dupuy and Rodrigo Figueroa Justiniano (2026). That paper establishes embedding guarantees for the global TTStack map. Using its partial suffix contractions inside TT-RS is an additional construction here, so the operator separately verifies the recursive left blocks and right-sketch dimensions required by CoreDeterminingSystem.

Parameters

  • tt_rank (int, optional) – Internal bond dimension of each random TT sketch.

  • stack_size (int, optional) – Number of independent TT sketches in each left or right stack.

  • orthogonal (bool, optional) – Whether to orthogonalize random cores toward their outgoing bond.

Examples

>>> operator = tk.decompositions.TTStackSketch(tt_rank=2, stack_size=3)
>>> operator.tt_rank * operator.stack_size
6

Sketching evaluation and extension objects#

These objects support transformations and custom sketches. Engines create their evaluation maps and Phi operators automatically.

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.ConfigurationMap(source, batch_size=64, transform=None)[source]#

Source values shared by all RSS queries and a global transformation.

RSS passes this object to transform(configuration_map) after evaluating the unique configurations needed by the local Phis. configurations contains these inputs directly, and values contains the aligned raw source values. Both tables keep their original shape and order while the callback runs. The callback returns transformed values with the same shape.

evaluate() can query additional configurations. It returns raw source values, preserving the requested order and repetitions, and evaluates only points absent from the shared cache. These auxiliary points do not change the initial tables or the sketch samples. Evaluation never recursively applies the transformation.

Instances are created by RSS; callbacks normally only read these properties and call evaluate(). Source input columns follow source.in_sites. Treat the exposed tables as read-only so cached raw evaluations remain available throughout the callback.

Examples

A symmetry average can evaluate new configurations in the callback:

def transform(configuration_map):
    inputs = configuration_map.configurations
    reflected = inputs.flip(1)
    return (configuration_map.values +
            configuration_map.evaluate(reflected)) / 2

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.PhiOperator(source, components, output_spec, *, input_sites=None, output_sites=None, input_kind=None)[source]#

Local source evaluations indexed by regional states and explicit axes.

Each component supplies one Phi axis: a RegionSketch contributes its unique regional configurations; (site, values) contributes the supplied values of one input or output variable. Components cover each represented variable exactly once. shape and layout describe this original indexing throughout the operator’s lifetime.

evaluate() and fiber() can query selected entries without constructing the complete tensor. materialize() fills tensor, initially None, and later queries reuse it. Clearing tensor drops that cache. fit() stores physical-basis coefficients and fitting diagnostics on this operator. truncate() updates coefficients and retains central lifting maps in left_lift and right_lift. These operations leave the original query coordinates and cache unchanged.

Parameters

  • source (BaseSource) – Source supplying the values. Structural source batches are not used by the sketching algorithms.

  • components (sequence of RegionSketch or tuple) – Regional configurations or (site, values) pairs, in Phi axis order. Explicit values have shape (n_values, *feature_shape); output variables contain scalar integer indices.

  • output_spec (_OutputSpec) – Output shape and placement in the represented chain.

  • input_sites (sequence of int, optional) – Represented variables supplied to the source, in source input order. Defaults to the input positions in output_spec.

  • output_sites (sequence of int, optional) – Represented output variables, in source output-axis order. Required with custom input_sites when the source has output axes.

  • input_kind ({"indices", "features"}, optional) – Meaning of input values. Inferred from the source or component values when omitted.

  • cutoff (float, optional) – Singular-value cutoff, absolute/relative discarded squared mass, or minimum retained squared mass, as in truncated_svd.

  • atol (float, optional) – Singular-value cutoff, absolute/relative discarded squared mass, or minimum retained squared mass, as in truncated_svd.

  • rtol (float, optional) – Singular-value cutoff, absolute/relative discarded squared mass, or minimum retained squared mass, as in truncated_svd.

  • cum_percentage (float, optional) – Singular-value cutoff, absolute/relative discarded squared mass, or minimum retained squared mass, as in truncated_svd.

  • projector (RangeProjector, optional) – Range-compression strategy before the local SVD.

  • generator (torch.Generator, optional) – Generator used by a randomized projector.

  • site (int, optional) – Global site index used to label truncation records.

  • collect_metrics (bool) – Whether to retain projection and truncation measurements.

Returns

This operator with updated coefficients, left_lift and right_lift. Original query coordinates and cache are unchanged.

Return type

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.CoreDeterminingSystem(phi, left_blocks, right_blocks, in_dim, operator, diagnostics=<factory>)[source]#

Stores local TT-RS tensors and recursive sketches in both directions.

phi[k] has shape (left_size[k], in_dim[k], right_size[k]). left_blocks[k] maps the left sketch through site k to the next left sketch. right_blocks[k] maps the right sketch through site k + 1 to the previous right sketch. The outer sketch sizes are one. These recursive maps let solve() start at any center.

The local equations follow Generative modeling via tensor train sketching (Hur, Hoskins, Lindsey, Stoudenmire and Khoo, 2022), Algorithms 1–4. Centered solves and explicit sparse support are TensorKrowch extensions of that construction.

Parameters

  • phi (sequence of torch.Tensor) – One three-axis local tensor per site.

  • left_blocks (sequence of torch.Tensor) – One tensor per cut, with shape (left_size[k + 1], in_dim[k], left_size[k]).

  • right_blocks (sequence of torch.Tensor) – One tensor per cut, with shape (right_size[k], in_dim[k + 1], right_size[k + 1]).

  • in_dim (sequence of int) – Input dimension for each tensor axis.

  • operator (str) – Name of the sketch operator used to build the system.

  • diagnostics (mapping, optional) – Additional construction information, copied into the result metadata.

solve(rank=None, *, center=None, cutoff=None, atol=None, rtol=None, cum_percentage=None, transform=None, range_projector=None, generator=None, strict_system=False, collect_metrics=False, _on_core=None)[source]#

Truncates local ranges and solves outward from center.

Each cut is selected by one local SVD, with both directions treated at the center. Singular values remain in the retained coefficients. Least-squares alignment with the recursive sketches then produces the TT cores. Ranks are neither padded nor rounded afterward.

Parameters

  • rank (int, sequence of int or None, optional) – Maximum rank at each TT cut. A sequence contains n_sites - 1 values. None discovers numerical ranks from the local SVDs.

  • center (int or None, optional) – Initial site. None selects the middle site.

  • cutoff (float or None, optional) – Truncation criteria passed to tensorkrowch.utils.truncated_svd(). With no rank or criterion, a numerical tolerance is used.

  • atol (float or None, optional) – Truncation criteria passed to tensorkrowch.utils.truncated_svd(). With no rank or criterion, a numerical tolerance is used.

  • rtol (float or None, optional) – Truncation criteria passed to tensorkrowch.utils.truncated_svd(). With no rank or criterion, a numerical tolerance is used.

  • cum_percentage (float or None, optional) – Truncation criteria passed to tensorkrowch.utils.truncated_svd(). With no rank or criterion, a numerical tolerance is used.

  • transform (callable or None, optional) – Applied to each three-axis Phi before its SVDs. Returns a tensor with the same shape; consistency between sites is the user’s responsibility.

  • range_projector (RangeProjector or None, optional) – Complete range-projection strategy. None applies SVD directly.

  • generator (torch.Generator or None, optional) – Generator used by a randomized range projector.

  • strict_system (bool, optional) – Raises if a local alignment matrix lacks full column rank.

  • collect_metrics (bool, optional) – Whether to collect truncation and local least-squares diagnostics.

Returns

Tensor train containing the aligned cores and diagnostics.

Return type

TTDecomposition

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.TensorDecomposition(cores, metrics=None, metadata=None, n_batches=0, **kwargs)[source]#

Historical fit diagnostics shared by decomposition results.

Combine this base with a numerical format, as in TTDecomposition or QTTDecomposition. The format owns the cores and numerical operations; metrics and metadata describe how the result was obtained. Editing cores does not rewrite these historical records. Use to_format() to work with the numerical format alone.

Parameters

  • cores (sequence of torch.Tensor) – Cores following the public layout of the concrete format.

  • metrics (DecompositionMetrics, optional) – Historical fit records; defaults to a new empty collection.

  • metadata (dict, optional) – Algorithm configuration; defaults to a new empty dictionary.

  • n_batches (int, optional) – Number of leading structural batch axes. Defaults to 0.

  • **kwargs – Additional constructor arguments of the concrete format.

Examples

Construct a concrete result combining this base with its numerical format:

>>> result = tk.decompositions.TTDecomposition(
...     [torch.tensor([1., 2.])], metadata={'algorithm': 'manual'})
>>> result.contract_dense()
tensor([1., 2.])
>>> result.as_info()['metadata']
{'algorithm': 'manual'}
as_info()[source]#

Returns current dimensions and historical decomposition diagnostics.

rank, in_dim and out_dim describe the current cores. Metrics describe the original fit, even after editing or rounding the result. Tensor-valued diagnostics are detached and moved to CPU by as_info().

Returns

Structure, a shallow copy of metadata and fit diagnostics.

Return type

dict

Examples

>>> result = tk.decompositions.TTDecomposition(
...     [torch.ones(2, 1), torch.ones(1, 3)],
...     metadata={'algorithm': 'manual'})
>>> info = result.as_info()
>>> info['in_dim'], info['rank']
([2, 3], [1])
>>> info['metadata']
{'algorithm': 'manual'}
error(*args, **kwargs)[source]#

Measures sample error for a vector decomposition result.

Evaluation follows error(), using the current cores. The returned record is detached and moved to CPU; historical records in metrics are not modified.

Parameters

  • function (callable) – Target function receiving samples and returning one value per data configuration, as a torch.Tensor.

  • samples (torch.Tensor or sequence of torch.Tensor) – Inputs to function, with n_batches leading data batch axes. A tensor groups sites on the next axis; a sequence contains one tensor per site. Quantics results require scalar coordinate or index inputs, without feature axes.

  • data (torch.Tensor or sequence of torch.Tensor, optional) – Inputs used to evaluate the format. Defaults to samples. Supply embedded inputs for generic vectors, or encoded digits when Quantics target samples are domain coordinates or grid indices.

  • n_batches (int, optional) – Number of leading data batch axes, independent of the structural batches stored in the cores. Defaults to 1.

  • **kwargs – Additional keyword arguments passed to function.

Returns

Absolute error, relative error, sample count and target norm, detached and stored on CPU. Errors include all samples and structural batches. The relative error divides the absolute error by the target norm. It is zero when both norms vanish and infinity when only the target norm vanishes.

Return type

ErrorRecord

Examples

>>> result = tk.decompositions.TTDecomposition(
...     [torch.tensor([1., 2.])])
>>> samples = torch.tensor([[0], [1]])
>>> def function(indices):
...     return indices[:, 0].float() + 1
>>> record = result.error(function, samples)
>>> record.absolute.item(), record.relative.item()
(0.0, 0.0)
to_format()[source]#

Returns the numerical format without decomposition diagnostics.

Cores, bond factors, Vidal information, vector orientation and the orthogonality center are preserved. Quantics results also retain their layouts and coordinate maps. metrics and metadata are omitted.

Core and bond containers are independent, but tensors are reused without cloning or detaching them. Replacing cores or bonds affects only the new format; editing shared tensor values affects both objects. Use clone() on the returned format when independent tensor storage is needed.

Returns

Corresponding TT, TR, TTM, TRM or Quantics format.

Return type

TensorFormat1D

Examples

>>> result = tk.decompositions.tt_svd(
...     torch.eye(2), rank=2)
>>> format = result.to_format()
>>> type(format)
<class 'tensorkrowch.formats.formats1d.TT'>
>>> format.contract_dense()
tensor([[1., 0.],
        [0., 1.]])
class tensorkrowch.decompositions.TTDecomposition(cores, metrics=None, metadata=None, n_batches=0, **kwargs)[source]#

TT with decomposition diagnostics.

The numerical API is inherited from TT. metrics and metadata describe the fit that produced the cores and remain historical when the result is modified. Use to_format() to obtain the corresponding TT without decomposition diagnostics.

Parameters

  • cores (sequence of torch.Tensor) – Core tensors following the public TT layout, with open boundaries. The container is copied; tensors retain storage and autograd.

  • metrics (DecompositionMetrics, optional) – Historical fit records; defaults to a new empty collection.

  • metadata (dict, optional) – Algorithm configuration; defaults to a new empty dictionary.

  • n_batches (int, optional) – Number of leading structural batch axes in each core, independent of data batches during evaluation. Defaults to 0.

  • bonds (sequence of torch.Tensor or None, optional) – Diagonal factors between cores. Defaults to None. Core and factor containers are copied; tensors are reused without cloning or detaching.

Examples

>>> cores = [torch.tensor([[1.], [2.]]), torch.tensor([[3., 4.]])]
>>> result = tk.decompositions.TTDecomposition(
...     cores, metadata={'algorithm': 'manual'})
>>> result.contract_dense()
tensor([[3., 4.],
        [6., 8.]])
>>> result.as_info()['rank']
[1]

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.QTTDecomposition(cores, metrics=None, metadata=None, n_batches=0, **kwargs)[source]#

QTT with decomposition diagnostics.

The numerical API is inherited from QTT. metrics and metadata describe the fit that produced the cores and remain historical when the result is modified. Use to_format() to obtain the corresponding QTT without decomposition diagnostics.

Coordinate evaluation follows the stored QuantizedLayout and CoordinateMap. Shorthand construction uses interleaved ordering, coarse_to_fine digits and an affine map with grid_offset="left" when domain is supplied.

Parameters

  • cores (sequence of torch.Tensor) – Core tensors following the public TT layout, with open boundaries. The container is copied; tensors retain storage and autograd.

  • n_coordinates (int) – Number of original coordinates. Required as a keyword argument.

  • base (int or sequence of int, optional) – Digit bases for shorthand construction. Required together with level and either domain or grid_coordinates.

  • level (int or sequence of int, optional) – Number of digits per coordinate for shorthand construction.

  • domain (torch.Tensor or sequence, optional) – Coordinate intervals used to construct an AffineCoordinateMap with grid_offset="left". Cannot be combined with grid_coordinates or prebuilt objects.

  • grid_coordinates (torch.Tensor or sequence, optional) – Domain grid points used to construct an ExplicitGridMap. A vector describes one coordinate; a matrix or sequence of vectors describes multiple coordinates. Each grid size must equal base ** level.

  • layout (QuantizedLayout, optional) – Prebuilt digit layout, supplied together with coordinate_map. Cannot be combined with shorthand construction arguments.

  • coordinate_map (CoordinateMap, optional) – Prebuilt map with grid sizes matching layout.grid_size.

  • metrics (DecompositionMetrics, optional) – Historical fit records; defaults to a new empty collection.

  • metadata (dict, optional) – Algorithm configuration; defaults to a new empty dictionary.

  • n_batches (int, optional) – Number of leading structural batch axes in each core, independent of data batches during evaluation. Defaults to 0.

  • bonds (sequence of torch.Tensor or None, optional) – Diagonal factors between cores. Defaults to None. Core and factor containers are copied; tensors are reused without cloning or detaching.

Examples

>>> cores = [torch.eye(2), torch.eye(2)]
>>> result = tk.decompositions.QTTDecomposition(
...     cores, n_coordinates=1, base=2, level=2, domain=(0., 1.),
...     metadata={'algorithm': 'manual'})
>>> coordinates = torch.tensor([[0.], [0.25], [0.75]])
>>> result.evaluate_coordinates(coordinates).tolist()
[1.0, 0.0, 1.0]
>>> result.to_format().contract_dense_grid_axes().tolist()
[1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0]

  • grid_coordinates (torch.Tensor or sequence, optional) – Domain grid points used to construct an ExplicitGridMap. A vector describes one coordinate; a matrix or sequence of vectors describes multiple coordinates. Each grid size must equal base ** level.

  • layout (QuantizedLayout, optional) – Prebuilt digit layout, supplied together with coordinate_map. Cannot be combined with shorthand construction arguments.

>>> cores = [torch.tensor([1., 2.]).reshape(1, 2, 1),

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.QTTMDecomposition(cores, metrics=None, metadata=None, n_batches=0, **kwargs)[source]#

QTTM with decomposition diagnostics.

The numerical API is inherited from QTTM. metrics and metadata describe the fit that produced the cores and remain historical when the result is modified. Use to_format() to obtain the corresponding QTTM without decomposition diagnostics.

Input and output coordinate spaces independently accept shorthand construction or a prebuilt QuantizedLayout and CoordinateMap. Their layouts must have equally many sites. Shorthand layouts use interleaved ordering and coarse_to_fine digits; affine maps use grid_offset="left".

Parameters

  • cores (sequence of torch.Tensor) – Core tensors following the public TTM layout, with open boundaries. The container is copied; tensors retain storage and autograd.

  • in_n_coordinates (int) – Number of original input and output coordinates. Both are required as keyword arguments.

  • out_n_coordinates (int) – Number of original input and output coordinates. Both are required as keyword arguments.

  • in_base (int or sequence of int, optional) – Digit bases for shorthand construction of each coordinate space. Each base requires its corresponding level and domain or grid points.

  • out_base (int or sequence of int, optional) – Digit bases for shorthand construction of each coordinate space. Each base requires its corresponding level and domain or grid points.

  • in_level (int or sequence of int, optional) – Number of digits per coordinate in each space.

  • out_level (int or sequence of int, optional) – Number of digits per coordinate in each space.

  • in_domain (torch.Tensor or sequence, optional) – Coordinate intervals used to construct affine maps with grid_offset="left". Cannot be combined with grid points or prebuilt objects for the same space.

  • out_domain (torch.Tensor or sequence, optional) – Coordinate intervals used to construct affine maps with grid_offset="left". Cannot be combined with grid points or prebuilt objects for the same space.

  • in_grid_coordinates (torch.Tensor or sequence, optional) – Domain grid points used to construct explicit maps. A vector describes one coordinate; a matrix or sequence of vectors describes multiple coordinates. Each grid size must equal the corresponding base ** level.

  • out_grid_coordinates (torch.Tensor or sequence, optional) – Domain grid points used to construct explicit maps. A vector describes one coordinate; a matrix or sequence of vectors describes multiple coordinates. Each grid size must equal the corresponding base ** level.

  • in_layout (QuantizedLayout, optional) – Prebuilt digit layouts, each supplied with its corresponding map. Both layouts must have the same number of sites.

  • out_layout (QuantizedLayout, optional) – Prebuilt digit layouts, each supplied with its corresponding map. Both layouts must have the same number of sites.

  • in_coordinate_map (CoordinateMap, optional) – Prebuilt maps with grid sizes matching their respective layouts. Cannot be combined with shorthand arguments for the same space.

  • out_coordinate_map (CoordinateMap, optional) – Prebuilt maps with grid sizes matching their respective layouts. Cannot be combined with shorthand arguments for the same space.

  • metrics (DecompositionMetrics, optional) – Historical fit records; defaults to a new empty collection.

  • metadata (dict, optional) – Algorithm configuration; defaults to a new empty dictionary.

  • n_batches (int, optional) – Number of leading structural batch axes in each core, independent of data batches during evaluation. Defaults to 0.

  • bonds (sequence of torch.Tensor or None, optional) – Diagonal factors between cores. Defaults to None. Core and factor containers are copied; tensors are reused without cloning or detaching.

Examples

>>> cores = [torch.eye(2).unsqueeze(1), torch.eye(2).unsqueeze(0)]
>>> result = tk.decompositions.QTTMDecomposition(
...     cores, in_n_coordinates=1, out_n_coordinates=1,
...     in_base=2, in_level=2, in_domain=(0., 1.),
...     out_base=2, out_level=2, out_domain=(-1., 1.),
...     metadata={'algorithm': 'manual'})
>>> in_coordinates = torch.tensor([[0.], [0.5]])
>>> out_coordinates = torch.tensor([[-1.], [0.5]])
>>> result.evaluate_coordinates(in_coordinates, out_coordinates).tolist()
[1.0, 0.0]
class tensorkrowch.decompositions.QTRMDecomposition(cores, metrics=None, metadata=None, n_batches=0, **kwargs)[source]#

QTRM with decomposition diagnostics.

The numerical API is inherited from QTRM. metrics and metadata describe the fit that produced the cores and remain historical when the result is modified. Use to_format() to obtain the corresponding QTRM without decomposition diagnostics.

Input and output coordinate spaces independently accept shorthand construction or a prebuilt QuantizedLayout and CoordinateMap. Their layouts must have equally many sites. Shorthand layouts use interleaved ordering and coarse_to_fine digits; affine maps use grid_offset="left".

Parameters

  • cores (sequence of torch.Tensor) – Core tensors following the public TRM layout, with a cyclic closure. The container is copied; tensors retain storage and autograd.

  • in_n_coordinates (int) – Number of original input and output coordinates. Both are required as keyword arguments.

  • out_n_coordinates (int) – Number of original input and output coordinates. Both are required as keyword arguments.

  • in_base (int or sequence of int, optional) – Digit bases for shorthand construction of each coordinate space. Each base requires its corresponding level and domain or grid points.

  • out_base (int or sequence of int, optional) – Digit bases for shorthand construction of each coordinate space. Each base requires its corresponding level and domain or grid points.

  • in_level (int or sequence of int, optional) – Number of digits per coordinate in each space.

  • out_level (int or sequence of int, optional) – Number of digits per coordinate in each space.

  • in_domain (torch.Tensor or sequence, optional) – Coordinate intervals used to construct affine maps with grid_offset="left". Cannot be combined with grid points or prebuilt objects for the same space.

  • out_domain (torch.Tensor or sequence, optional) – Coordinate intervals used to construct affine maps with grid_offset="left". Cannot be combined with grid points or prebuilt objects for the same space.

  • in_grid_coordinates (torch.Tensor or sequence, optional) – Domain grid points used to construct explicit maps. A vector describes one coordinate; a matrix or sequence of vectors describes multiple coordinates. Each grid size must equal the corresponding base ** level.

  • out_grid_coordinates (torch.Tensor or sequence, optional) – Domain grid points used to construct explicit maps. A vector describes one coordinate; a matrix or sequence of vectors describes multiple coordinates. Each grid size must equal the corresponding base ** level.

  • in_layout (QuantizedLayout, optional) – Prebuilt digit layouts, each supplied with its corresponding map. Both layouts must have the same number of sites.

  • out_layout (QuantizedLayout, optional) – Prebuilt digit layouts, each supplied with its corresponding map. Both layouts must have the same number of sites.

  • in_coordinate_map (CoordinateMap, optional) – Prebuilt maps with grid sizes matching their respective layouts. Cannot be combined with shorthand arguments for the same space.

  • out_coordinate_map (CoordinateMap, optional) – Prebuilt maps with grid sizes matching their respective layouts. Cannot be combined with shorthand arguments for the same space.

  • metrics (DecompositionMetrics, optional) – Historical fit records; defaults to a new empty collection.

  • metadata (dict, optional) – Algorithm configuration; defaults to a new empty dictionary.

  • n_batches (int, optional) – Number of leading structural batch axes in each core, independent of data batches during evaluation. Defaults to 0.

  • bonds (sequence of torch.Tensor or None, optional) – Diagonal factors between cores. Defaults to None. Core and factor containers are copied; tensors are reused without cloning or detaching.

Examples

>>> cores = [torch.eye(2).reshape(1, 2, 1, 2) for _ in range(2)]
>>> result = tk.decompositions.QTRMDecomposition(
...     cores, in_n_coordinates=1, out_n_coordinates=1,
...     in_base=2, in_level=2, in_domain=(0., 1.),
...     out_base=2, out_level=2, out_domain=(-1., 1.),
...     metadata={'algorithm': 'manual'})
>>> in_coordinates = torch.tensor([[0.], [0.5]])
>>> out_coordinates = torch.tensor([[-1.], [0.5]])
>>> result.evaluate_coordinates(in_coordinates, out_coordinates).tolist()
[1.0, 0.0]

class tensorkrowch.decompositions.LocalSolveRecord(environment_shape, target_shape, driver, abs_residual, rel_residual, effective_l2_reg=0.0, column_scaling=False, site=None, sweep=None, sampling_exact=None, sample_generation=None)[source]#

Stores the outcome of one local least-squares solve.

Residuals describe the original local data equations, before numerical scaling and without the regularization penalty. Scalar tensors are detached and stored on CPU. Fixed solver configuration belongs to the solver; this record retains effective choices that can vary between solves.

Parameters

  • environment_shape (tuple[int, int]) – Shape (n_rows, n_parameters) of the local design matrix.

  • target_shape (tuple[int, ...]) – Right-hand-side shape (n_rows,) or (n_rows, n_targets).

  • driver (str) – Effective least-squares driver, including any CPU retry.

  • abs_residual (torch.Tensor) – Norm of the local residual.

  • rel_residual (torch.Tensor) – Residual norm divided by the target norm. A zero target gives zero for an exact fit and infinity otherwise.

  • effective_l2_reg (torch.Tensor) – Regularization coefficient after relative or environment rescaling. Defaults to zero.

  • column_scaling (bool) – Whether this solve balanced its columns. Defaults to False.

  • site (int or tuple[int, ...], optional) – Site or block identifier.

  • sweep (int, optional) – Directional sweep identifier.

  • sampling_exact (bool, optional) – Whether the sampling proposal matches the current local design.

  • sample_generation (int, optional) – Generation of the sampled rows.

Compatibility helpers#

These historical model-construction functions emit deprecation warnings. Use the numerical decomposition interfaces for new code.

tensorkrowch.decompositions.vec_to_mps(vec, n_batches=0, rank=None, cutoff=None, atol=None, rtol=None, cum_percentage=None, renormalize=False, verbose=0, return_info=False)[source]#

Compatibility wrapper for tt_svd().

Deprecated since version 1.2: Use tt_svd() for TT terminology, explicit output-device policy and repeated fits through TTSVD.

The historical vec and n_batches arguments are preserved. Final cores remain on the input device, matching the previous behavior. The tensor should have shape (*batch_shape, d_1, ..., d_n), where each non-batch axis is the input dimension of one TT site.

Parameters

  • vec (torch.Tensor) – Dense tensor to decompose.

  • n_batches (int) – Number of leading tensor axes interpreted as batch dimensions.

  • rank (int, optional) – Maximum rank allowed at every link. At each SVD cut, at most this many singular values are retained.

  • cutoff (float, optional) – Minimum singular value to keep. It must be finite and non-negative. Singular values <= cutoff are removed.

  • atol (float, optional) – Absolute tolerance over the tail sum of squared singular values. Starting from the smallest singular value, values are discarded while the accumulated sum of squares is <= atol. It must be finite and non-negative.

  • rtol (float, optional) – Relative tolerance over the tail sum of squared singular values. Starting from the smallest singular value, values are discarded while the tail sum of squares divided by the total sum of squares is <= rtol. It must be finite and in [0, 1].

  • cum_percentage (float, optional) –

    Minimum fraction of squared singular-value mass to keep. Equivalent to setting rtol = 1 - cum_percentage. It must be finite and in [0, 1].

    \[\]
    frac{sum_{i in {kept}}{s_i^2}}{sum_{i in {all}}{s_i^2}} ge

    cum_percentage

  • renormalize (bool) – If True, normalizes each residual and accumulates its scale logarithmically before redistributing it over the final cores.

  • verbose (bool or int) – Console verbosity level forwarded to tt_svd().

  • return_info (bool) – If True, returns (cores, info) with ranks, dimensions, metadata and structured metrics.

Returns

TT cores, optionally followed by their structured information.

Return type

list[torch.Tensor] or tuple

Examples

The canonical replacement only changes the function and tensor argument names:

>>> tensor = torch.arange(16.).reshape(2, 2, 2, 2)
>>> cores = tk.decompositions.tt_svd(tensor, rank=2).cores
>>> [tuple(core.shape) for core in cores]
[(2, 2), (2, 2, 2), (2, 2, 2), (2, 2)]
tensorkrowch.decompositions.mat_to_mpo(mat, rank=None, cutoff=None, atol=None, rtol=None, cum_percentage=None, renormalize=False, verbose=0, return_info=False)[source]#

Compatibility wrapper for ttm_svd().

Deprecated since version 1.2: Use ttm_svd() for TTM terminology, grouped or matrix layouts, explicit output-device policy and repeated fits through TTMSVD.

The historical mat argument and interleaved ordering are preserved. Final cores remain on the input device, matching the previous behavior. mat should have shape (in_1, out_1, ..., in_n, out_n).

Parameters

  • mat (torch.Tensor) – Dense tensor with interleaved input/output dimensions.

  • rank (int, optional) – Maximum rank allowed at every link. At each SVD cut, at most this many singular values are retained.

  • cutoff (float, optional) – Minimum singular value to keep. It must be finite and non-negative. Singular values <= cutoff are removed.

  • atol (float, optional) – Absolute tolerance over the tail sum of squared singular values. Starting from the smallest singular value, values are discarded while the accumulated sum of squares is <= atol. It must be finite and non-negative.

  • rtol (float, optional) – Relative tolerance over the tail sum of squared singular values. Starting from the smallest singular value, values are discarded while the tail sum of squares divided by the total sum of squares is <= rtol. It must be finite and in [0, 1].

  • cum_percentage (float, optional) –

    Minimum fraction of squared singular-value mass to keep. Equivalent to setting rtol = 1 - cum_percentage. It must be finite and in [0, 1].

    \[\]
    frac{sum_{i in {kept}}{s_i^2}}{sum_{i in {all}}{s_i^2}} ge

    cum_percentage

  • renormalize (bool) – If True, normalizes each residual and accumulates its scale logarithmically before redistributing it over the final cores.

  • verbose (bool or int) – Console verbosity level forwarded to ttm_svd().

  • return_info (bool) – If True, returns (cores, info) with ranks, dimensions, metadata and structured metrics.

Returns

TTM cores, optionally followed by their structured information.

Return type

list[torch.Tensor] or tuple

Examples

To preserve the historical ordering with the canonical API, construct an interleaved source explicitly:

>>> tensor = torch.arange(16.).reshape(2, 2, 2, 2)
>>> source = tk.decompositions.DenseTensorSource.matrix(
...     tensor, ordering="interleaved")
>>> cores = tk.decompositions.ttm_svd(source, rank=2).cores
>>> [tuple(core.shape) for core in cores]
[(2, 2, 2), (2, 2, 2)]
